before.best_for: Smart presentation slides that auto-format as you add content
before.description: Beautiful.ai is a presentation tool whose current release, Beautiful.ai 3.0 "Create with AI" (March 2026), turns slide-making into a context-aware, conversational AI workflow. It is now a paid product with a 14-day trial and no permanent free plan.
before.description_long:
Beautiful.ai is a web-based presentation app built around "smart slides" that automatically adjust layout, spacing and alignment as you add content, so decks stay tidy without manual fiddling. It has always leaned toward design automation rather than freehand slide editing.

The current version, Beautiful.ai 3.0 "Create with AI," shipped in March 2026 and reframes the product around a context-aware, conversational AI workflow. Instead of only auto-redesigning slides, you now describe what you want and refine it through iterative chat, with faster prompt-to-deck generation, AI image generation and AI-assisted theme selection.

The 3.0 update also added localization in 15 languages, a new public API and a ChatGPT app, plus a more mobile-friendly experience. Around the same time the company raised a $45M investment from General Catalyst and introduced flat-rate SMB plans (SMB 50 at $6,000/yr for up to 50 users, SMB 100 at $12,000/yr for up to 100 users).

Pricing runs from Pro at $12/user/month billed annually ($144/yr) or $50/month monthly, to Team (2-20 users) at $40/user/month annually or $50/user/month monthly, up to custom Enterprise pricing for 20+ users. There is also a one-off Single Presentation option at $45, and students get one year free with a .edu email.

The main limitation is cost and access: Beautiful.ai retired its old free plan, so beyond the 14-day trial (and the one-year education offer) there is no perpetual free tier. The design-automation model also means less pixel-level control than PowerPoint or Google Slides.

It fits professionals and teams who want good-looking, on-brand decks quickly and are happy to trade fine-grained manual control for speed and consistency, especially those who will actually use the AI generation and template automation.

before.description: Claude Code is Anthropic's AI coding agent, now at CLI v2.1.x (June 2026) with Claude Opus 4.8 as the default model. It runs across terminal, web and mobile, and can drive cloud agents, subagents and computer use.
before.description_long:
Claude Code is Anthropic's agentic coding tool. It reads your codebase, edits files, runs commands and can carry a task from a plain-language request through to a working change, rather than just suggesting completions in an editor.

The current release is CLI v2.1.x (v2.1.185-v2.1.193, late June 2026). Since May 28, 2026 the default model has been Claude Opus 4.8, Anthropic's strongest computer-use and browser-agent model, which runs at high effort by default (you can push it further with /effort xhigh). Fast mode now also runs on Opus 4.8 at $10/$50 per million tokens, roughly 3x cheaper than the models it replaced.

Beyond the terminal, Claude Code spans web and mobile. Recent additions include 'dynamic workflows' that orchestrate dozens to hundreds of subagents, expanded Auto mode (now on the Pro plan and on Bedrock, Google Cloud and Microsoft Foundry), computer use in the CLI, /ultrareview cloud bug-hunting, Artifacts (beta), scheduled cloud agents (Routines), native Windows support without Git Bash, /code-review and background subagents.

Pricing: the Free tier ($0) does not include Claude Code. It is bundled into Pro ($17/mo annual or $20/mo monthly), Max 5x (from $100/mo), Max 20x ($200/mo), Team Premium ($100/seat/mo annual, $125 monthly, 5-seat minimum) and Enterprise (seat plus API-rate usage from $20/seat). Team Standard is $20/seat/mo annual ($25 monthly). API access is priced separately at an intro $2/$10 per million tokens through Aug 31, 2026, then $3/$15; Opus 4.8 fast mode is $10/$50.

Limitations are worth knowing. There is no free way to use it, usage caps still apply even on paid plans (Anthropic doubled limits on May 6, 2026 and added pay-as-you-go overage with a spend cap), and API usage can get expensive on large agentic runs. High-effort agent runs can also be slow and consume tokens quickly.

It suits professional developers and teams who want an agent that actually edits and ships code, especially those already on a Claude Pro, Max or Team plan who want coding included without a separate API bill.

before.description_long:
Cursor is an AI-first code editor that started as a VS Code fork and has grown into a full agentic coding platform. Instead of just autocompleting lines, it can plan and carry out multi-step changes across a repository, run its own review passes, and hand work off to background agents.

The current release is Cursor 3.10, shipped June 30, 2026. The headline change is Composer 2.5, Cursor's own in-house agentic model introduced in May 2026, which the company positions as matching frontier models like Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5 at roughly a tenth of the cost. Version 3.10 added team marketplaces and Team MCP servers, while 3.9 brought an iOS app (public beta) and a customization hub. The project also moved its home from cursor.sh to cursor.com.

Key capabilities include the Composer agent for large edits, cloud agents and cloud dev environments you can trigger with /in-cloud, automatic code review, and a faster, cheaper Bugbot that returns reviews in around 90 seconds. It still supports third-party models, MCP servers, custom rules, and hooks, so you are not locked into Composer.

Pricing is tiered. Hobby is free, Pro (Individual) is $20 per month, Pro+ is $60 per month, and Ultra is $200 per month; Teams costs $40 per user per month and Enterprise is custom. Billing is credit-based, with a credit pool roughly equal to the plan price, though Auto mode usage is unlimited on paid plans. Annual billing saves about 20 percent.

The main limitations are cost and complexity. Heavy agent use can burn through credits quickly, and the pricing model has changed enough over time to confuse users. Being a VS Code fork, it occasionally lags behind upstream extensions, and the most capable features assume you are comfortable letting an agent make sweeping changes.

Cursor suits developers who want an agent that can take on real multi-file tasks, not just suggest snippets. It is a strong fit for professional teams already living in VS Code, and less compelling for people who only want lightweight autocomplete or work in a non-VS-Code editor.

before.description: Fireflies.ai is an AI meeting assistant that records, transcribes and summarizes calls across Zoom, Google Meet, Teams and more. It now runs on a dynamic AI Credits system that gates advanced features like AskFred, Voice Agents and CRM autofill, with paid plans starting at $10/user/mo (annual).
before.description_long:
Fireflies.ai is a meeting-notetaker platform. Its bot joins your video calls, transcribes the conversation, and produces searchable notes, summaries and action items you can share with your team or push into other tools.

There is no public version number because Fireflies is a continuously updated SaaS. The biggest recent change is the move to a dynamic AI Credits model: advanced and AI-driven features now consume credits per query based on complexity, and each plan includes a fixed monthly credit pool. Alongside this, Fireflies added Voice Agents, AI Skills, Sales Assist, a Slack Assistant, CRM autofill and a Personal Assistant. The transcription and Q&A assistant is branded Fred / AskFred.

Core capabilities include automatic recording and transcription, AI summaries and topic tracking, keyword and speaker search across your meeting history, an AskFred assistant you can query about past calls, and integrations that autofill CRM fields or post to Slack. Creating your first Voice Agent grants a one-time 100-credit bonus valid for 14 days.

Pricing has four tiers. Free costs $0 and includes 20 AI credits per month; the live pricing page now lists 400 minutes of storage per team, though Fireflies own knowledge base still cites 800 minutes per seat, so the exact figure is currently inconsistent. Pro is $10/user/mo billed annually (or $18 monthly) with 8,000 minutes per seat and 20 credits. Business is $19/user/mo annual (or $29 monthly), unlimited storage and 30 credits, and is marked Most Popular. Enterprise is $39/user/mo annual only, unlimited storage, 50 credits, plus SSO, SCIM, HIPAA and audit logs. Add-on credit bundles run roughly $0.06 to $0.10 per credit.

The main limitation to understand is that advanced AI features are now metered: even paid plans get a modest monthly credit pool (20 to 50), so heavy AskFred, Voice Agent or automation use can require paid top-ups. The Free plan's storage number is currently ambiguous between Fireflies own pages.

Fireflies suits teams that run many meetings and want automatic notes, searchable transcripts and CRM/Slack automation, especially sales and customer-facing groups. If you only need occasional transcription, the credit caps and metering may feel restrictive.

It runs on a dynamic AI Credits system that gates advanced features like AskFred, Voice Agents and CRM autofill, with paid plans starting at $10/user/mo billed annually (or $18/user/mo billed monthly).
after.description_long:
Fireflies.ai is a meeting-notetaker platform. Its bot joins your video calls, transcribes the conversation, and produces searchable notes, summaries and action items you can share with your team or push into other tools.

There is no public version number because Fireflies is a continuously updated SaaS. The biggest recent change is the move to a dynamic AI Credits model: advanced and AI-driven features now consume credits per query based on complexity, and each plan includes a fixed monthly credit pool. Alongside this, Fireflies added Voice Agents, AI Skills, Sales Assist, a Slack Assistant, CRM autofill and a Personal Assistant. The transcription and Q&A assistant is branded Fred / AskFred.

Core capabilities include automatic recording and transcription, AI summaries and topic tracking, keyword and speaker search across your meeting history, an AskFred assistant you can query about past calls, and integrations that autofill CRM fields or post to Slack.

Pricing has four tiers. Free costs $0 forever and includes unlimited transcription (asterisked), limited AI summaries, 400 minutes of storage per team per month, and 20 AI credits. Pro is $10 per seat per month billed annually (or $18 per seat per month billed monthly), with 8,000 minutes of storage per seat and 20 AI credits. Business is $19 per seat per month billed annually (or $29 per seat per month billed monthly), with unlimited storage and 30 AI credits, and is marked Most Popular. Enterprise is $39 per seat per month, billed annually only, with unlimited storage, 50 AI credits, plus SSO, SCIM, HIPAA and audit logs.

The main limitation to understand is that advanced AI features are now metered: even paid plans get a modest monthly credit pool (20 to 50), so heavy AskFred, Voice Agent or automation use can require additional credits. The lowest advertised prices also require annual billing, and Enterprise has no monthly option at all.

Fireflies suits teams that run many meetings and want automatic notes, searchable transcripts and CRM/Slack automation, especially sales and customer-facing groups. If you only need occasional transcription, the free plan's storage cap and the credit metering on paid plans may feel restrictive.

before.best_for: AI video generation, native audio, image-to-video, 4K upscaling
before.description: Google's text- and image-to-video model, now shipping as Veo 3.1 with synchronized dialogue, sound effects and ambient audio. Since April 2026 it is free for all personal Google accounts through Google Flow and Google Vids, with paid Pro/Ultra and API tiers for higher volume.
before.description_long:
Google Veo is Google's generative video model. You describe a scene in text or feed it a still image, and it produces short cinematic clips, now with matching audio baked in rather than added afterwards.

The current version is Veo 3.1, which replaced Veo 3 around the end of March 2026. The update added a cheaper Veo 3.1 Lite tier alongside the Fast and Standard variants, and improved the synchronized audio so clips can include spoken dialogue with lip-sync, sound effects and ambient background. In April 2026 Google made Veo 3.1 free for every personal Google account through Flow and Vids, which is the single biggest change for casual users.

On capability, Veo 3.1 handles both text-to-video and image-to-video, produces clips up to 8 seconds, and generates audio in the same pass. It is available inside Google Flow (the dedicated video tool) and Google Vids, and through the Vertex AI and Gemini APIs for developers.

Pricing has a genuine free path: any personal Google account gets Veo 3.1 in Flow (roughly 50 daily AI credits, about 12 clips a day) and in Vids (around 10 clips a month), capped at 8-second clips. Paid subscriptions run about $7.99/mo for Google AI Plus, $19.99/mo for AI Pro and $249.99/mo for AI Ultra. On the API, Veo 3.1 Fast is about $0.15 per second and Standard about $0.40 per second, audio included.

The main limitations are the short 8-second clip length, daily and monthly caps on the free tier, and the fact that top quality and volume still sit behind paid plans. Output quality and prompt adherence also vary from generation to generation.

Veo 3.1 suits creators, marketers and hobbyists who want quick, audio-complete video clips without buying anything up front, and teams who can move to Pro/Ultra or the API when they need more throughput.

Veo 3.1 suits developers who want predictable per-second, per-resolution API billing, and teams already on a Google AI subscription who need audio-complete video clips inside Flow or the Gemini app. It is not a fit for anyone looking for a no-cost way to generate video.

before.description: Krea AI is a web-based creative suite for AI image generation, now built around Krea 2, the company's first from-scratch foundation model (May 2026), plus the ~2-second Krea 2 Turbo. Alongside images it covers video, 3D, and 8K upscaling.
before.description_long:
Krea AI started as a real-time image generation tool and has grown into a full creative platform that runs in the browser. It combines its own models with a large library of third-party ones, so you can move between styles and tasks without leaving the app.

The headline change is Krea 2, released in May 2026 as the company's first foundation image model built from scratch, a roughly 12B-parameter Diffusion Transformer. It was quickly followed in June by Krea 2 Turbo, which produces high-quality images in about two seconds. Krea also shipped open-weights versions of K2 Raw and K2 Turbo under a custom license.

On top of the base models, Krea 2 adds Generative Sliders for direct control over intensity, complexity, movement, and prompt creativity, LoRA training so you can teach it your own style or subject, a Moodboard Gallery, and a Krea 2 API. The wider suite now includes text- and image-to-video, 3D generation, 8K AI upscaling, and more than 64 integrated models.

Pricing is tiered. The free plan costs nothing and gives 100 compute units per day with no card required. Basic is $9/month ($5.40 on annual billing) with 5,000 units and a commercial license. Pro is $35/month ($21 annual) with 20,000 units, all video models, and 8x concurrency. Max is $70/month ($42 annual) with 60,000 units and unlimited concurrency. Business runs $200/month with 80,000 units, up to 50 seats, and SSO, and Enterprise is custom. Annual billing is about 40% off.

The main limits are practical. Everything is metered in compute units, so heavy use of video, 3D, or upscaling can burn through an allowance quickly, and the free daily cap is modest. The sheer number of models and controls also makes the interface busy for newcomers.

Krea fits people who want one place for image, video, 3D, and upscaling rather than separate tools, and who value fast iteration and fine-grained control. It is less suited to anyone who only needs occasional single images and would rather not think about a credit system.

before.best_for: Enterprise agents, Microsoft ecosystem
before.description: Microsoft Copilot Studio is a low-code platform for building and deploying custom AI agents that connect to Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365 and external systems. The 2026 release wave 1 (platform build 2026.6.2) adds general-availability computer-using agents, a new orchestration layer, real-time voice agents and a choice of models including GPT-5.5 Reasoning and Anthropic Claude Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.5.
before.description_long:
Microsoft Copilot Studio is Microsoft's low-code environment for designing, testing and publishing AI agents. It sits inside the Power Platform and Microsoft 365 ecosystem, letting makers wire agents to enterprise data, Teams, Dynamics 365 and third-party APIs without heavy custom code.

The current version is 2026 release wave 1, running on platform build 2026.6.2 (June 2026). This wave brought several substantial changes: computer-using agents reached general availability, and a new orchestration layer improves accuracy on evaluations by roughly 20% while cutting token consumption by about 50%. Real-time speech-to-speech voice agents were added for Dynamics 365 Contact Center, and multi-step workflows were redesigned so UI-driven agents run alongside API actions and approvals.

On the capability side, the platform now supports multi-agent orchestration, autonomous computer-using agents and a broader model choice. In the Prompt Tool you can select GPT-5.5 Reasoning (early release) or Anthropic Claude Opus 4.8 and Sonnet 4.5, offered as a paid experimental preview in the US.

Pricing runs entirely on Copilot Credits, which replaced the old per-message billing on September 1, 2025 (same quantity and rate). A prepaid capacity pack is $200 per pack per month for 25,000 Copilot Credits; pay-as-you-go is metered at $0.01 per credit with no upfront commitment but requires an Azure subscription. A one-year Copilot Credit Commit Units (CCCU) prepurchase can save up to 20%. Building agents is included at no extra cost with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license at $30 per user per month, billed annually.

The main limitation is that there is no free production tier. The free authoring or maker license costs $0 but only works if the tenant already holds a paid prepaid Copilot Credit pack, and the individual free trial license is time-limited and cannot publish agents. In practice, deploying anything requires payment.

Copilot Studio suits organizations already invested in Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365 or Azure that want governed, low-code agents connected to their existing data. It is a weaker fit for individuals or small teams wanting a genuinely free way to ship an agent to production.

before.best_for: AI meeting transcription, video replay, sales intelligence, CRM sync
before.description: Otter.ai is a voice-productivity platform that in 2026 repositioned from a passive meeting notetaker into an agentic Conversational Knowledge Engine, adding voice-activated AI agents for meetings, sales, and demos alongside its transcription roots. Its current release centers on the Otter Meeting Agent plus a rebuilt, private-by-default AI Chat.
before.description_long:
Otter.ai started life as a real-time transcription service for meetings and interviews, turning spoken conversations into searchable, shareable notes across Zoom, Google Meet, and Microsoft Teams. That capability is still at the core, and for many people it remains the main reason to use the product.

The big shift came in April 2026, when Otter announced the Otter Meeting Agent and rebranded the whole product as a Conversational Knowledge Engine. Instead of quietly transcribing in the background, Otter now fields voice-activated AI agents: the Meeting Agent joins calls, answers questions, and completes tasks using a company's accumulated meeting data; the Sales Agent offers real-time coaching and objection handling on live calls; and the SDR Agent is a multimodal agent that can autonomously run product demos.

Enterprise is custom-priced and adds SSO, SCIM, an optional HIPAA add-on, and API access. Students with a .edu address get 20% off Pro.

The limitations are worth knowing. The free tier's minute and import caps are tight for regular use, the most compelling agent features sit behind Business and Enterprise, and letting an AI agent actively participate in meetings raises real privacy and accuracy questions that not every team or client will accept. Transcription quality also still varies with accents, audio quality, and crosstalk.

Otter suits sales teams, customer-facing organizations, and knowledge workers who run many meetings and want an assistant that not only records but retrieves and acts on that history. If you only need occasional, straightforward transcription, the free or Pro tier covers it without touching the agent layer.

before.best_for: Instant AI background removal from photos and product images
before.description: Remove.bg is a Canva-owned AI tool that automatically removes backgrounds from images. There is no public version number; it runs a proprietary background-removal engine offered through free low-resolution previews plus a credit-based model for full-resolution downloads.
before.description_long:
Remove.bg is a specialized web service and API that isolates the subject of a photo and strips out the background in a single step. It is owned by Canva (through Kaleido) and is aimed at people who need clean cutouts for product shots, portraits, and marketing graphics without opening an image editor.

There is no public version numbering, and nothing fundamental has changed recently. The tool still runs the same proprietary AI engine and keeps the long-standing three-option structure: free previews, subscriptions, and pay-as-you-go credits. Ownership remains with Canva, and there has been no shift from free to paid or paid to free.

In practice you upload an image or paste a URL and get an automatic cutout in a few seconds. It handles hair, fur, and semi-transparent edges reasonably well, supports transparent PNG output, and offers a browser tool, desktop and mobile apps, an API, and integrations with tools like Photoshop and Canva.

Pricing is built around credits. A free account gives you low-resolution web previews up to 0.25 MP, one bonus high-resolution credit, and 50 API or app previews per month. Pay-as-you-go credits never expire and cost roughly $0.20 per image at standard rates, dropping at higher volumes. Subscriptions, whose credits roll over while active, run about $9/month for 40 credits, $39/month for 200 credits, up to a Volume+ tier around $80/month for roughly 500 credits, with enterprise pricing above about 100,000 images a year. All paid plans include a 14-day money-back guarantee.

The main limitation is that the free tier is genuinely a preview: downloads are capped at 0.25 MP, so any full-resolution result requires paid credits. Complex edges, busy backgrounds, and low-contrast subjects can still need manual touch-ups, and the per-image cost adds up for large batches.

Remove.bg suits e-commerce sellers, marketers, and designers who need fast, consistent cutouts at scale and are comfortable paying per image or by subscription for full-resolution output.

before.description: Suno is an AI music generator that turns a text prompt into a full song with vocals and instruments. The current flagship model is v5.5 (released March 26, 2026), which sits behind the paid tiers, while the free plan is limited to the older v4.5-all model.
before.description_long:
Suno is a text-to-music tool that writes, arranges and performs a song from a short description or your own lyrics. You type a prompt, pick a style, and it returns finished tracks with vocals and backing instrumentation in about a minute.

The headline model right now is v5.5, launched on March 26, 2026. It introduced Voices, which let you clone or reuse your own singing voice; Custom Models, which fine-tune v5.5 to your own back catalogue (up to three per account, on Pro and Premier); and My Taste, which learns the genres and moods you gravitate toward. Note that v5 and v5.5 are paid-only, so the free tier still runs on the older v4.5-all model.

Day to day, the tool covers the full loop: generation from a prompt, custom lyrics, style and persona control, stem separation on paid plans, and audio upload to extend or remix existing material.

Pricing runs on a credit system where one full song costs 5 credits. Free gives you $0/mo and 50 credits per day, which works out to roughly 10 songs a day, for personal, non-commercial use only, with no stem separation and 8-minute uploads. Pro is $10/mo (or $8/mo billed annually, $64/yr) for 2,500 credits a month (about 500 songs), the v5.5 model, commercial rights, personas, two stem types, 30-minute uploads and a priority queue. Premier is $30/mo (or $24/mo annually, $192/yr) for 10,000 credits (about 2,000 songs), v5.5, Suno Studio, commercial use and three stem types.

The main limitations are that the newest quality is gated: you cannot touch v5.5, stem separation or commercial rights on the free plan, and the daily free allowance is smaller than it first appears once you account for 5 credits per song.

Suno suits hobbyists experimenting with ideas, content creators who need cleared background music, and musicians who want fast demos or reference tracks, provided they are willing to pay for the current model and commercial use.

before.description: AI coding IDE formerly known as Windsurf, rebranded to Devin Desktop on June 2, 2026 after Cognition acquired Codeium. Its default agent is now Devin Local, with the new free in-house model SWE-1.6.
before.description_long:
Devin Desktop is an AI-native code editor that grew out of Codeium and Windsurf. It combines an autocomplete engine (Tab), inline edits, and an autonomous coding agent inside a familiar VS Code-style workspace.

The product changed a lot in 2026. Cognition acquired Codeium/Windsurf for roughly $250M and rebranded the IDE to Devin Desktop on June 2, 2026. Both windsurf.com and codeium.com now redirect to devin.ai. The original Cascade agent reached end-of-life on July 1, 2026 and was replaced by Devin Local as the default agent, and new users start in agent mode by default.

On the model side, SWE-1.6 is the current free proprietary model. Paid tiers also open up access to OpenAI, Anthropic Claude and Google Gemini models, plus Devin cloud agents and Devin Review, which handle longer background tasks and automated code review.

Pricing was reworked on March 19, 2026: the old credit system was retired in favor of daily and weekly quotas. Free is $0/mo with a light quota, unlimited Tab completions and inline edits, and limited model access. Pro is $20/mo (up from $15) with full model access, free SWE-1.6 and cloud agents. A new Max tier is $200/mo with much higher quotas. Teams costs $80/mo base plus $40/mo per developer seat, and Enterprise is custom. Annual billing saves roughly 17-20%, and students get about 50% off Pro.

The main caveats are churn and lock-in: the rapid rebrand, the retirement of Cascade, and the shift to quotas mean workflows and limits have moved more than once in a single year. Heavy agent use can burn through quotas quickly, and much of the value now sits behind the Devin ecosystem.

It suits developers who want an agent-first editor with strong autocomplete and are comfortable inside the Cognition/Devin ecosystem. Anyone tied to older Windsurf/Cascade branding or the credit model should be aware those are gone.

after.description_long:
Devin Desktop, formerly known as Windsurf, is an AI-native code editor built by Cognition. It combines an autocomplete engine (Tab), inline edits, and autonomous coding agents inside a VS Code-style workspace. Windsurf for JetBrains continues to be offered under the original Windsurf name.

The product was renamed from Windsurf to Devin Desktop on June 2, 2026, after Cognition and Windsurf came together. windsurf.com and codeium.com/windsurf now redirect to devin.ai/desktop. The in-editor agent picker currently lists several selectable agents, including Devin Local, Codex, Claude Agent, OpenCode and Cascade, so the original Cascade agent is still available rather than retired.

On the model side, SWE-2 is the current in-house model, released September 10, 2026, replacing the earlier SWE-1.6. Paid tiers also unlock access to models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, SpaceXAI, and leading open-source models, along with Devin Cloud agents for longer background tasks and Devin Review for automated code review.

Pricing runs on daily and weekly quotas rather than the older credit system. Free is $0 per month with a light agent quota, limited model access, and unlimited Tab completions and inline edits. Pro is $20 per month with increased quotas, full model access, Devin Cloud agents, up to 10 concurrent sessions, and free use of SWE-2 through October 16, 2026 as a limited-time offer. Max is $200 per month with significantly higher quotas. Teams costs $80 per month as a base plus $40 per month per developer seat for up to 200 users, and Enterprise pricing is custom with SSO and VPC deployment.

The main caveats are churn and lock-in: the rebrand from Windsurf to Devin Desktop, and the move from credits to quotas, mean workflows and limits have shifted within the same year. Heavy agent use can burn through quotas quickly, and the free access to SWE-2 on Pro is time-limited rather than permanent. Much of the product's value now sits behind the Devin ecosystem.

It suits developers who want an agent-first editor with strong autocomplete and are comfortable working inside the Cognition/Devin ecosystem. Anyone still looking for the original Windsurf branding or credit-based pricing should know those have changed, though Windsurf branding persists in the JetBrains plugin.

before.description_long:
Bolt.new is a browser-based AI app builder that generates and deploys full-stack web applications from natural language prompts. The original Bolt gained attention in 2024 for generating frontend code quickly; Bolt V2, also called Bolt Cloud, is a substantially deeper platform with built-in infrastructure that eliminates the need to configure third-party services.

Bolt Cloud bundles everything needed for a production web app: a built-in database, authentication system, file storage, edge functions, analytics, and hosting — all managed within the Bolt platform. Users do not need to set up Supabase, Firebase, or any separate backend service. This integrated stack is the most significant architectural difference between Bolt and competitors like Lovable or Replit.

MCP (Model Context Protocol) support allows Bolt to connect external tools — Notion, Linear, Git repositories, and other MCP-compatible services — directly into the generation workflow. This makes it possible to build apps that read from a Notion database, update Linear issues on completion, or commit generated code to a Git repository automatically.

AI image generation is built into the chat interface, with WebP export for use in generated applications. Build performance has improved by 40% compared to the 2024 version, and Bolt now handles projects approximately 1,000 times larger than the original — making it viable for serious applications rather than just prototypes.

Team features include shared workspaces, team templates, admin controls, and collaborative editing, enabling multiple developers or stakeholders to work on the same Bolt project. Claude Opus 4.8 is available as a model option with adjustable reasoning intensity, allowing users to trade response speed for deeper architectural thinking on complex generation tasks.

Bolt.new is best for developers and founders who want to build and ship full-stack applications without managing separate hosting, auth, and database services, and for teams that need collaborative AI app development in a single platform.

before.description_long:
Claude Design is a design-focused assistant from Anthropic Labs. Rather than being a standalone product, it is a feature bundled into paid Claude subscriptions, aimed at turning existing project material into polished, consistent design output.

It launched on April 17, 2026 as a research preview and runs on the Claude Opus 4.7 vision model. Note that while the broader Claude line moved to Opus 5 in mid-2026, there is no official confirmation that Claude Design itself has been upgraded past 4.7.

The core idea is that Claude Design can read a team's codebase and design files and use them to auto-build a reusable design system. From there it exports finished work to Canva, PDF, PPTX or standalone HTML, and can hand off directly to Claude Code for implementation.

There is no standalone price. Access is included with paid Claude plans and metered against each plan's usage limits: Pro at $20/mo ($17/mo billed annually), Max 5x at $100/mo, Max 20x at $200/mo, Team Standard at $25/seat/mo ($20 annual), Team Premium at $125/seat/mo ($100 annual), and Enterprise on custom pricing. The Free $0 plan does not include Claude Design.

Usage is tracked separately and counts against your subscription limits, and users report fairly restrictive weekly caps; you can purchase extra usage beyond those limits. Being a research preview, behavior and availability may change.

It suits product teams and designers already on a paid Claude plan who want to generate a consistent design system from existing code and files, and who value a smooth handoff into Claude Code.

before.description_long:
DeepL is a machine-translation service known for producing natural, context-aware output rather than word-for-word conversions. It handles text, full documents, and integrates into browsers and desktop apps, and it now includes an AI writing assistant (DeepL Write) for grammar and phrasing.

The big shift in 2026 is that DeepL no longer relies on generic models. It runs a purpose-built next-generation translation LLM, first launched in 2024 and heavily expanded through 2025-2026, which DeepL says wins the large majority of blind quality comparisons against general-purpose models. Language coverage jumped to 100+ languages via a 70+ language rollout, and DeepL Voice-to-Voice real-time translation arrived around April 2026.

Capabilities span quick text translation, whole-document translation that preserves formatting, glossaries and tone controls, the Write assistant for polishing text, and API access for developers who want translation inside their own products.

Pricing is tiered. Free costs nothing and gives roughly 50,000 characters per month plus one document (5MB cap). Individual (Pro) is $8.74/mo billed annually with 300,000 characters and three documents. Team is $28.74/user/mo annually (1M characters), and Business is $57.49/user/mo annually with unlimited fair-use volume and Write Pro included. Write Pro is a +$7.49/user/mo add-on on lower tiers. The API has a free tier (500,000 chars/mo) and a Pro plan at $5.49/mo plus $25 per million characters. Annual billing runs about 16% cheaper than monthly.

Limitations are worth noting: the free tier's monthly character and document caps are tight for regular work, the best writing features sit behind add-ons, and language coverage, while much wider now, still trails the biggest general-purpose models for rarer pairs.

DeepL suits people and teams who translate regularly and care about output that reads naturally: professional translators, localization teams, and businesses handling multilingual documents and customer communication.

before.description_long:
Flux is a family of image generation and editing models built by Black Forest Labs. It spans several variants aimed at different needs, from top-quality API models to open-weight versions you can run yourself.

The current generation is FLUX.2, which launched in late 2025 and replaced the older FLUX.1 line. The lineup now includes FLUX.2 [pro], [flex], [max], [dev] and, since January 2026, the compact [klein] model (offered in 4B and 9B sizes). Klein handles both generation and editing, runs on consumer GPUs with around 13GB of VRAM, and delivers sub-second inference; NVIDIA and ComfyUI FP8 optimizations cut VRAM use by roughly 40%.

On capabilities, FLUX.2 supports multi-reference input (up to about 10 reference images) for character and style consistency, photorealistic output up to 4 megapixels, a context window of around 32k tokens, and strong text rendering that reaches roughly 92% accuracy on complex layouts.

Pricing is pay-as-you-go and billed per megapixel, with no subscriptions or seats. FLUX.2 [pro] costs $0.03 for the first megapixel then $0.015 per additional MP (reference images $0.015/MP); [max] is around $0.07 first MP then ~$0.03/MP; [klein] is about $0.014 first MP then ~$0.001/MP. Legacy FLUX.1 [pro] tiers ran roughly $0.04-0.06/MP.

The open-weight side is where the free option lives. FLUX.1 [schnell] is Apache 2.0 and fine for commercial use; FLUX.1 [dev] is non-commercial; FLUX.2 [dev] and [klein] ship with open weights. Commercial self-hosting above certain volumes requires a paid Open Weights license (Builder up to 10K img/mo, Platform/Professional up to 100K, Enterprise custom).

Flux suits developers and studios who want either the best possible photorealism through an API or a self-hostable model they can fine-tune and control, and who are comfortable with per-megapixel billing or license management.

before.description: Grammarly is an AI writing assistant for grammar, clarity, tone and rewriting that works across the web and desktop apps. Since late 2025 it is part of the Superhuman suite, with prompt-based AI generation and the proactive Superhuman Go agent alongside the classic checker.
before.description_long:
Grammarly is a writing assistant that checks spelling, grammar, punctuation, clarity and tone, and can rewrite or generate text with AI. It runs in the browser, as a desktop app, in Microsoft Office and mobile keyboards, so the same suggestions follow you across almost any text field.

The product changed significantly in late 2025. On November 5, 2025 the company that made Grammarly rebranded itself to Superhuman, bringing Grammarly (writing), Coda (documents and workspace) and Superhuman Mail together under one name. Grammarly is now positioned as an AI-native writing and agent platform rather than a standalone grammar checker.

Alongside the rebrand, the company launched Superhuman Go, a proactive AI assistant that can act across more than 100 connected apps, and opened a closed developer beta of the Superhuman Agents SDK. The plan lineup was also consolidated: the former standalone Business tier was folded into Pro.

Key capabilities include real-time grammar and style corrections, tone detection, full-sentence rewrites, plagiarism checking, and prompt-driven AI generation measured in monthly AI prompts. It supports mainly US, UK, Canadian and Australian English.

Pricing is freemium. The Free plan costs $0 and includes 100 AI prompts per month plus core corrections. Pro is around $12 per member per month billed annually (roughly $30 month-to-month) with 2,000 AI prompts per month and a 7-day trial. Enterprise is custom-priced with admin and security controls.

The main limitations: it is English-centric, the monthly AI prompt caps can be reached quickly by heavy users, some rewrite suggestions still need human judgment, and the browser extension can feel intrusive in certain editors. It fits students, professionals, non-native English writers and teams who want consistent, on-the-fly writing help across their tools.

before.description_long:
Lindy is a platform for building and running AI agents that act on your behalf. Rather than exposing numbered releases, it ships continuously, so there is no public version number to track. What matters more is what the product has become.

In the first quarter of 2026 Lindy went through a significant repricing and repositioning. It relaunched as a consumer-facing 'AI executive assistant' rather than a purely developer-oriented agent builder, and it retired its old free plan (which had offered roughly 400 credits a month). The whole lineup was replaced by paid Plus, Pro and Max tiers, per-tier credit numbers were dropped from the public page, and the pricing is now framed against the cost of a human assistant, cited at around $8,000 a month.

On capability, Lindy connects to email, calendars, iMessage/SMS, meeting notes and more than 100 integrations, and can chain these into multi-step automations. The Pro and Max tiers add model selection (choosing among underlying frontier LLMs) and computer use, letting agents operate a browser and interact with apps that lack a clean API.

Pricing is paid-only after a 7-day free trial that needs no credit card. Plus is $49.99/mo with standard usage and up to two inboxes; Pro is $99.99/mo with roughly triple the usage, up to three inboxes, plus computer use and model selection; Max is $199.99/mo with about seven times the usage and up to five inboxes. Enterprise is custom-priced and adds SSO, SCIM, HIPAA and audit logs. Usage is credit-based on top of the base plan, and overages are billed at roughly double the standard rate.

The main limitations are cost and predictability. The free tier is gone, entry starts at $49.99/mo, and because published credit allowances were removed it can be hard to estimate what a given workload will actually cost, especially once overages kick in at about 2x. Annual pricing is not published.

Lindy suits professionals and small teams who want an assistant that actually takes actions across their inbox, calendar and tools, and who are comfortable paying assistant-tier prices. It is a poor fit for anyone who needs a genuinely free option or wants fully transparent, fixed usage costs up front.

before.description_long:
Perplexity is a conversational search tool that answers questions with cited, up-to-date sources instead of a list of links. It sits somewhere between a chatbot and a search engine, and over 2026 it has leaned hard into research and agentic work.

The headline change is Advanced Deep Research. It is no longer a simple multi-page report mode: it now runs agentically inside Perplexity Computer, asks clarifying questions before it starts, accepts follow-ups mid-run, and shows live source and progress tracking. On Pro and Max, Deep Research is powered by Claude Opus 4.7 and Sonnet 4.6, and Perplexity reports state-of-the-art benchmark scores (93.9% on SimpleQA, 21.1% on Humanity's Last Exam). The Deep Research in Computer agentic assistant shipped on June 19, 2026, adding a command panel, thread forking, inline actions, analytics APIs, and enterprise credit controls.

Beyond research, Perplexity gives you multi-model access to the GPT-5.6 family, Claude Opus 5, Gemini and other frontier models, a Model Council feature that compares several models side by side, and the Comet browser for AI-assisted browsing.

Pricing runs across five tiers. Free is $0 and includes roughly 5 Pro searches per day. Pro is $20/mo or $200/yr, bundles $5/mo of Sonar API credits, and allows about 20 Deep Research runs a day. The new Max tier is $200/mo or $2,000/yr and adds Model Council, 10,000 Computer credits a month, Sora 2 Pro video and Nano Banana Pro image generation, and unlimited Labs. Students get Pro for around $10/mo, and there are Enterprise Pro (~$40/seat/mo) and Enterprise Max (~$325/seat/mo) plans.

before.description_long:
Runway is a web-based generative media platform built around text-to-video and image-to-video, but it has grown well beyond a simple editor. Today it also handles image generation and native audio, and it hosts a range of third-party models alongside its own.

The current flagship is Gen-4.5, announced on December 1, 2025. It sits at the top of the Gen-4 family, which also includes Gen-4 and the faster Gen-4 Turbo. Compared with earlier Gen-4 models, Gen-4.5 improves motion quality, prompt adherence, and physical and temporal realism, and the family added native audio generation alongside video. At launch it took the No. 1 spot on the Artificial Analysis Video Arena leaderboard.

Beyond its own models, Runway lets you work with external ones such as Veo 3.1, Nano Banana Pro, Kling 3.0, Seedance 2.0, and Gemini, so you can compare outputs without leaving the platform. That makes it useful for character consistency across shots, image-driven video, and mixed image, video, and audio workflows.

Pricing is credit-based. The Free plan costs nothing and gives 125 one-time credits with watermarked output and limited models (no Gen-4 Video, Gen-4.5, or Veo). Standard is $12/mo billed annually ($15 monthly) with 625 credits a month. Pro is $28/mo annually ($35 monthly) with 2,250 credits. Max is $76/mo annually ($95 monthly) with 9,500 credits and one-month rollover; it replaced the discontinued Unlimited plan. Enterprise pricing is custom.

The main limitation is the credit system: generation consumes credits, so heavy use gets expensive, and the free tier is more of a trial than a working plan. The new Max plan is purely credit-based and, unlike the old Unlimited plan, does not include Explore Mode.

Runway suits creators, editors, and studios who want a single place to generate and compare AI video across multiple models, and who are comfortable paying per credit for higher-quality output.

before.best_for: AI Search Optimization, brand monitoring in AI, content refreshing
before.description: SurferSEO is a marketing platform that has shifted from classic on-page content optimization toward AI-search visibility, tracking how brands are mentioned across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI and Gemini, alongside its Surfy AI assistant and content humanizer.
before.description_long:
SurferSEO started as an on-page SEO tool built around a Content Editor that scored draft articles against the pages already ranking in Google, giving writers a checklist of terms, headings and length targets to hit.

As of mid-2026 the product has repositioned around Generative Engine Optimization (GEO). The headline capability is now tracking brand and page mentions inside AI answer engines such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI and Gemini, rather than only Google's blue links. There is no numbered version; Surfer ships continuously.

Alongside the AI-visibility tracking, Surfer added Surfy, a built-in AI assistant, and an AI content humanizer meant to make machine-drafted text read less obviously generated. The older Content Editor, keyword research and audit tools remain part of the suite.

Pricing was renamed and restructured into Discovery at $49/mo, Standard at $99/mo, Pro at $182/mo, Peace of Mind at $299/mo (all billed yearly), plus a custom Enterprise tier. Plan value is now defined largely by the number of tracked AI prompts rather than just the count of Content Editor articles.

The main limitations are cost, which climbs quickly for teams that need more tracked prompts, and the fact that the GEO metrics are still a young discipline where methodology and reliability are evolving. The AI humanizer also does not guarantee content will pass every detector.

Surfer suits content teams, agencies and in-house marketers who already do serious SEO work and now want to measure and influence how they show up in AI-generated answers, not just traditional search results.

before.best_for: No-code web application builder with full database and logic support
before.description: Bubble is a no-code platform for building web and native mobile (iOS/Android) apps visually, now with AI-assisted app generation and usage-based Workload-Units pricing.
before.description_long:
Bubble is a visual development platform that lets you build full web applications without writing code. You design the interface by dragging elements onto a canvas, model your data in a built-in database, and wire up logic through a point-and-click workflow editor.

As a continuously updated SaaS, Bubble has no version numbers, but the platform has changed significantly of late. It now includes a native mobile app builder that publishes to iOS and Android, AI-assisted app generation that scaffolds apps from prompts, and a reworked pricing model based on Workload Units (WU) that meter server-side usage rather than fixed capacity.

Key capabilities include a responsive visual editor, a relational database, reusable components, an API connector for third-party services, a plugin marketplace, and one-click deployment. The AI generation feature can produce a starting app that you then refine by hand.

Pricing is split into three tracks. Web-only paid plans run Starter $29/mo, Growth $119/mo, and Team $349/mo (billed annually). Mobile-only plans are $42, $169, and $449. Web+Mobile combined plans are $59, $209, and $549. Enterprise is a custom quote. The free plan is $0 with 50K Workload Units and one editor but is deployment-locked to prototyping only, with no live app or custom domain.

The main limitations are cost predictability and lock-in. Workload-Units billing can spike with traffic or inefficient workflows, and everything you build lives inside Bubble's proprietary environment, so migrating off the platform means rebuilding. Complex or high-scale apps can also hit performance ceilings.

Bubble suits founders, small teams, and agencies who want to ship a real web or mobile product without hiring developers, validate an idea quickly, or build internal tools. It is less suited to teams that need full control over their code or expect very high, unpredictable traffic.

before.description: DeepSeek is a Chinese AI chat assistant now running on DeepSeek-V4 (released April 24, 2026), offered free through its web interface and as a paid, per-token API.
before.description_long:
DeepSeek is a conversational AI assistant from the Chinese lab of the same name. You can talk to it for free at chat.deepseek.com, or build on top of it through a metered API that charges per million tokens. It handles general chat, coding, reasoning, and long-document work.

The current generation is DeepSeek-V4, whose preview launched on April 24, 2026 and replaced the older V3/R1 family. It ships in two tiers: V4-Pro (1.6 trillion total parameters, 49 billion active) aimed at competing with top closed-source models, and the cheaper default V4-Flash (284 billion total, 13 billion active). The legacy deepseek-chat and deepseek-reasoner model names are being deprecated on July 24, 2026.

Key capabilities include a new DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA) mechanism with token-wise compression for better efficiency, a standard 1M-token context window with output up to 384K tokens, and explicit agentic optimizations, including integration with agent tools such as Claude Code.

On pricing, the web chat is free. The API is paid, per 1M tokens: V4-Flash costs $0.14 input on a cache miss ($0.0028 on a cache hit) and $0.28 output; V4-Pro costs $0.435 input on a cache miss ($0.003625 on a cache hit) and $0.87 output. The legacy names map to V4-Flash's non-thinking and thinking modes.

Limitations to keep in mind: the API is a metered, paid service rather than free access, some third-party reports of a free token grant for new accounts are not confirmed in official documentation, and as a China-based service it may raise data-residency or compliance questions for some organizations.

DeepSeek suits developers who want a strong, low-cost model API, and casual users who want a capable free web assistant without a subscription.

after.description_long:
DeepSeek is a conversational AI assistant from the Chinese lab of the same name. It offers a web chat interface at chat.deepseek.com alongside a metered API that developers can build on. It handles general chat, coding, reasoning, and long-document work.

The API currently serves two model families: deepseek-flash, now on the V4.1-Flash architecture released September 10, 2026 with a native multimodal design, and deepseek-v4-pro, which reached general availability on August 13, 2026. Older model names such as deepseek-chat and deepseek-reasoner no longer appear on the pricing page; legacy aliases deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp are still accepted but now route to V4.1-Flash. DeepSeek has iterated on its model lineup rapidly over the past few months, so names and pricing have changed more than once in a short period.

Both models offer a 1M-token context window with output up to 384K tokens, and a default thinking mode with selectable low, high, and max reasoning effort. Vision input is supported on deepseek-flash but not on deepseek-v4-pro. DeepSeek documents agent integrations including Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and its own DeepSeek Harness.

API pricing is billed per 1 million tokens and varies by peak and off-peak UTC hours, with off-peak priced at half the peak rate. Peak hours are 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC, Monday to Friday, excluding Chinese public holidays. For deepseek-flash: input on a cache miss is $0.15 off-peak / $0.30 peak, input on a cache hit is $0.003 off-peak / $0.006 peak, and output is $0.60 off-peak / $1.20 peak. The pricing page also references a 'granted balance' used before any topped-up balance, but does not explain how or when it is granted. Pricing for the web chat interface could not be confirmed on a primary page at time of writing.


Limitations to keep in mind: whether the web chat remains free could not be re-verified today, the 'granted balance' mechanism is unclear, concurrency is capped at 2,500 requests for deepseek-flash and 500 for deepseek-v4-pro, vision is Flash-only, the model lineup has changed several times in recent months, and as a China-based service it may raise data-residency or compliance questions for some organizations.

DeepSeek suits developers who want a low-cost, long-context API for coding, reasoning, or high-volume tasks, and who are comfortable tracking peak/off-peak pricing and occasional model migrations.

before.description: Grok is xAI's conversational AI, integrated with X and available at grok.com. The current flagship is Grok 4.5, available through SuperGrok plans and also offered inside third-party tools such as GitHub Copilot.
before.description_long:
Grok is the chat assistant built by xAI, Elon Musk's AI company. It lives both inside X (formerly Twitter) and as a standalone product at grok.com, and it is known for a looser, more opinionated conversational style than most rivals, plus tight access to real-time posts on X.

The flagship model is Grok 4.5 (Beta), which became the default in April 2026. It improved tool-calling and has since been superseded by Grok 4.5, which carries a 500k-token context window and a February 2026 knowledge cutoff. xAI has announced Grok 4.5 for public release on July 9, 2026, pitched as an "Opus-class" model built on a new 1.5-trillion-parameter V9 foundation and trained partly on Cursor coding data.

On capabilities, Grok handles text chat, image and video understanding, web and X search, and image/video generation through Grok Imagine. Developers can also reach the models through the xAI API.

Pricing spans a wide ladder. The free tier is $0 and now runs a lighter Grok 4 Mini, text only, capped at roughly 10 prompts every 2 hours. Paid options include X Premium at $8/mo, SuperGrok Lite at $10/mo, SuperGrok at $30/mo (or $300/yr, about 17% off), X Premium+ at $40/mo, and SuperGrok Heavy at $300/mo. The API (grok-4.3) costs $1.25 per million input tokens and $2.50 per million output tokens.

The main limitation is the free tier, which was tightened in March 2026: image and video generation were removed from it and it only runs Grok 4 Mini with a tight prompt cap. Getting the full flagship experience and Grok Imagine requires a paid plan.

Grok suits people already active on X who want an assistant wired into live posts, users who like a more candid tone, and developers who want a competitively priced API. Anyone who needs the newest model or heavy image/video generation should expect to pay.

before.best_for: AI logo and brand identity generation for small businesses
before.description: Looka is an AI logo maker and branding tool. Its 2026 release adds faster, more accurate logo generation, animated logo videos, multilingual prompts, custom color palettes, a rebuilt text editor, and a native iOS app; you design and preview logos for free and pay only to download.
before.description_long:
Looka is an online design platform built around an AI logo maker. You answer a few questions about your company name, industry and style preferences, and it generates a range of logo concepts you can refine in a browser-based editor without any design experience.

The 2026 version is a meaningful step up rather than a cosmetic refresh. Looka rolled out a faster and more accurate AI generation engine, added animated logo videos for YouTube intros, social posts and presentations, introduced multilingual prompt input, and now lets you feed a custom color palette into the generation so results match your brand from the start. There's also an all-new text and font editor, a revamped Explore inspiration section, and a dedicated iOS app called Looka AI Logo Maker Generator.

On the design side you can edit fonts, colors, layout, spacing and icons, save unlimited versions, and preview your logo on mockups. The Brand Kit turns your chosen logo into hundreds of matched marketing templates, and the top tier can even generate a hosted website using your branding.

Pricing has two shapes. One-time logo packages: Basic Logo at $20 gives a single low-resolution PNG, while Premium Logo at $65 unlocks high-resolution PNG, EPS, SVG and PDF files, color variations, unlimited edits after purchase and full ownership. Annual subscriptions add Brand Kit at $96/year (300+ branded assets and templates plus unlimited logo changes) and Brand Kit + Web at $129/year, which adds an AI-generated website with hosting.

The key limitation is that designing, previewing and saving are free, but downloading any usable file requires a purchase, and the cheapest option is only a low-res PNG. Output also tends toward clean, template-influenced styles, so highly bespoke or hand-crafted identities may still need a human designer.

Looka suits founders, small businesses and side projects that need a professional-looking logo and consistent brand assets quickly and cheaply, without hiring an agency.

before.description: Mistral's consumer AI assistant, rebranded from Le Chat to Vibe on June 5, 2026 and now powered by Mistral Medium 3.5 (128B parameters, 256k context). It splits into three modes: Vibe Chat for conversation, Vibe Work for agent workflows, and Vibe Code for cloud coding agents.
before.description_long:
Vibe is the consumer-facing AI assistant from French lab Mistral. It started life as Le Chat and, on June 5, 2026, was rebranded to Vibe; the URL, your login, and all existing plans and conversations carried over, so nothing was lost in the switch.

The current version runs on Mistral Medium 3.5, a 128B-parameter model with a 256k-token context window, released in public preview with open weights under a modified MIT license. This is a clear shift from the earlier framing as a fast multilingual chatbot toward a more agent-oriented product.

Vibe is now built around three modes. Vibe Chat is the classic turn-based conversation, essentially the old Le Chat. Vibe Work is an agent mode with persistent memory that executes multi-step workflows across connected tools, asking for your approval before it takes sensitive actions. Vibe Code provides remote coding agents that run asynchronously in the cloud and let you move a session from your local machine to the cloud.

Pricing has a free tier at $0/mo with limited features and models. Pro is $14.99/mo, Team is $24.99 per user/mo (billed monthly, with a $50/mo minimum and 30GB of storage per user), and Enterprise is custom-priced with private deployments and custom models, UI and tools. Verified students get an Education plan at $5.99/mo, valid for up to 12 months. You can pay in USD or EUR.

Worth knowing: the Vibe consumer subscription is billed separately from Mistral's developer API, so a Pro or Team plan does not include API credits. Medium 3.5 is also still in public preview, which means some rough edges are expected.

Vibe suits people who want a European-built assistant with open weights, and teams that want agentic workflows and cloud coding agents rather than a plain chatbot. If you only need occasional Q&A, the free tier may be enough.

before.best_for: Step-by-step math problem solving from camera or typed input
before.description: Photomath is a Google-owned math app that scans handwritten or printed problems with your phone camera and shows step-by-step solutions. It now runs as a cloud-based Google product with AI-powered animated tutorials, and there is no formal published version number.
before.description_long:
Photomath is a mobile app for solving math problems by pointing your camera at them. It reads handwritten and printed equations, returns the answer, and walks you through how to get there one step at a time. It covers arithmetic, fractions, algebra, trigonometry, calculus and more.

Since becoming part of Google, Photomath no longer publishes a formal version number and operates as a cloud-based Google product. The current focus is on AI: more than 400 AI-powered animated tutorials with voiceover, deeper explanations, contextual hints in the Plus tier, ongoing expansion toward college-level topics, and closer ties to Google Lens and the Gemini assistant. Support now lives on support.google.com/photomath.

Core capabilities include camera scanning, a built-in smart calculator, multiple solving methods for many problems, and animated walkthroughs that explain the reasoning rather than just handing over an answer.

Pricing is freemium. The core app is free with unlimited step-by-step solutions, camera scan and calculator, no ads and no time limit. Photomath Plus costs $9.99 per month or $69.99 per year (about $5.83/month, roughly 50% off), with a six-month option in some markets and a 7-day free trial. Plus adds the animated tutorials, richer explanations and contextual hints.

Limitations are worth noting. Handwriting recognition can misread messy notation, word problems remain harder than clean equations, the deepest teaching content sits behind the paywall, and being tied to Google now means your account and data flow through Google's ecosystem.

Photomath suits students who want to understand method, not just copy answers, as well as parents helping with homework and anyone who needs to check work quickly. If you only want a final number, a plain calculator is enough; Photomath earns its place when you want the steps.

before.best_for: Academic research with smart citations — see if papers support or contradict each other
before.description: Scite is an AI research assistant built around Smart Citations, which show whether later papers support or contradict a claim. As of 2026 it has expanded well beyond citation analysis, adding an MCP integration that plugs its 250M+ article library into ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, Cursor and Claude Code.
before.description_long:
Scite is a research tool that started as a way to see how a scientific paper has been cited. Instead of a raw citation count, its Smart Citations tell you whether each citing paper supports, mentions or contradicts the original claim, which makes it easier to judge how well a finding has held up.

The product is continuously updated rather than versioned. The most significant recent change came in February 2026 with the launch of the Scite MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration, which lets Scite work inside ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, Cursor and Claude Code. From those tools you can search over 250 million articles, evaluate results with Smart Citations and pull full-text PDFs. The same release removed data caps on chats and saved searches, added newer AI models to the Assistant while retiring older ones, and introduced AI Report Summaries. In March 2026 Scite added the ability to paste DOIs straight into the Assistant, save up to five named settings presets, drag citation popups around, and expanded MCP coverage to patents, clinical trials and grants.

before.description_long:
Synthesia is a browser-based tool for creating videos from a written script. You pick an avatar, type or paste your text, choose a voice, and the platform renders a presenter-style video without cameras, actors or studio time. It is used mainly for training material, product explainers, internal communications and localized marketing.

The current version is Synthesia 3.0, built around the Express-2 avatar engine (Expressive Model 4.0). This is a diffusion-transformer model that generates full-body avatars with natural hand and body movement rather than static talking heads. Version 3.0 also added Veo 3 integration for AI-generated B-roll, interactive Video Agents, Express-Voice instant voice cloning, and enhanced AI Dubbing with frame-accurate lip sync.

The avatar catalog has grown to 180+ stock avatars on the Creator plan and up to 240+ on Enterprise. Personal avatars can now be created from a single image, and lower tiers include a smaller but still usable set of presenters and voices in over 140 languages.

Pricing is tiered. The free Basic plan costs $0/mo and gives you 10 minutes of video per month, 9 AI avatars and 3 personal avatars, with a watermark. Starter is $29/mo monthly or $18/mo billed annually (10 min/mo, 125+ avatars, 3 personal avatars, logo removal, downloads, AI Dubbing). Creator, the most popular plan, is $89/mo monthly or $64/mo annually (30 min/mo, 180+ avatars, 5 personal avatars, API access, interactive videos). Enterprise is custom-priced with unlimited minutes, 240+ avatars, unlimited personal avatars, SAML/SSO and SCORM export. Synthesia recently cut its prices, with Starter down roughly 38%.

The main limitations are the monthly minute caps, which are tight on lower plans, and the fact that avatar-led video suits explanatory content far better than cinematic or emotionally nuanced storytelling. Rendering and editing quirks still occur, and the most advanced features sit behind Creator and Enterprise.

Synthesia is a strong fit for L&D teams, HR, product marketing and anyone who needs to produce or localize a high volume of talking-head videos quickly and without a film crew. It is less suited to creators chasing highly produced, cinematic output.

before.description: Zapier is a workflow automation platform that connects 8,000+ apps and, in its 2026 platform, has become AI-first: Zapier Copilot builds and maintains automations from plain language, while Zapier Agents act autonomously and Zapier MCP exposes 30,000+ actions to external LLMs like Claude and GPT.
before.description_long:
Zapier is a cloud automation service that links the apps you already use so data and tasks move between them without manual copy-paste. You build workflows called Zaps, which run on triggers and actions, and you can also create Tables, Interfaces, and Chatbots inside the same account.

The current 2026 platform marks a clear shift toward AI. Zapier Copilot (now in beta on every plan) turns plain-language descriptions into working Zaps, Tables, Interfaces, Chatbots, and Agents, and the 2026 release added agent checkpoints and one-click undo so you can review and roll back what the AI does. Zapier Agents are autonomous AI teammates that take action without waiting for a trigger, and Zapier MCP exposes more than 30,000 actions to outside models such as Claude and GPT.

On capabilities, integration coverage grew to 8,000+ apps (Copilot reaches 9,000+), on top of multi-step Zaps, filters, paths, formatting, webhooks, and the data and interface tools that make Zapier closer to a lightweight app builder than a simple connector.

Pricing is freemium. The Free plan is $0/mo with 100 tasks per month, two-step Zaps, and Copilot Beta. Professional starts at $19.99/mo billed annually ($29.99 monthly) with 750 base tasks that scale with volume. Team starts at $69/mo for 25 users, with higher task tiers reported around $103.50/mo, and Enterprise is custom. The AI products are priced separately: Agents (Free 400 activities/mo, Pro $33.33/mo, Enterprise custom) and Chatbots (Free 2 bots, Pro $13.33/mo, Advanced $66.67/mo, plus Custom).

The main limitation is cost at scale: tasks are metered, and busy workflows or the separately billed AI products can add up quickly. Advanced logic can get fiddly, and the newer Agents and Copilot features still benefit from human review before you trust them unattended.

Zapier fits teams and solo operators who want to automate across many SaaS tools without code, and who want AI to draft and maintain those automations. If you need only one or two heavy, high-volume pipelines, a cheaper task model elsewhere may serve you better.

before.description: Adobe Firefly is a standalone generative AI creative studio for image, video, and audio, now running on Firefly Image Model 5 (GA March 2026) with native 4MP output and access to 30+ partner models.
before.description_long:
Adobe Firefly began as the AI generation engine inside Photoshop and Illustrator, but it has grown into a standalone creative studio on the web and in dedicated apps. It now spans image, video, and audio generation rather than just still images, and it keeps the commercial-safe positioning Adobe built its reputation on.

The headline change is Firefly Image Model 5, which reached general availability in March 2026. It generates natively at 4MP without a separate upscaling step, and Adobe reports improved photorealism and anatomy over earlier models. It also introduces Prompt to Edit, a conversational way to edit an existing image, plus custom style models, with Layered Image Editing still in private beta.

Beyond Adobe's own models, Firefly now acts as an aggregator: it hosts more than 30 third-party models, including Google Nano Banana 2, Veo 3.1, Runway Gen-4.5, and Kling 2.5 Turbo. That lets you switch between Adobe and partner engines for image, video, and audio work inside one interface.

Pricing runs across four tiers. Free is $0/month with 25 generative credits, where every generation consumes a credit. Firefly Standard is $9.99/month with 2,000 premium credits plus unlimited standard generations. Firefly Pro is $19.99/month with 4,000 premium credits, and Firefly Premium is $199.99/month with 50,000 premium credits. On paid plans credits are only spent on premium features like video, audio, and partner models; standard image tools such as Text to Image and Generative Fill are unlimited.

The main limitation is the credit economy. On the free tier a credit is burned by every single generation, so 25/month goes quickly, and heavier video or partner-model use eats premium credits fast even on paid plans. Some newer features, like Layered Image Editing, are still gated behind private beta.

Firefly suits designers and content teams who want commercially safe generation, and anyone already inside Adobe's ecosystem who wants image, video, and audio plus multiple partner models under one subscription.

It suits solo creators, small marketing teams, social media managers, and non-designers who want good-looking, on-brand assets fast without learning a professional design tool.

before.description: ComfyUI is an open-source, node-based visual editor for building image and video generation pipelines with diffusion models. The current release, v0.27.0 (June 30, 2026), adds int8 quantized model support and new workflow nodes, and the project now also offers the managed Comfy Cloud service alongside the free self-hosted app.
before.description_long:
ComfyUI is a graph-based interface for running diffusion models. Instead of a single prompt box, you wire together nodes (loaders, samplers, conditioning, upscalers and so on) into a workflow you can inspect, reuse and share. That transparency is the reason it became the go-to tool for people who want precise control over how an image or video is generated.

The current version is v0.27.0, released on June 30, 2026. It adds int8 quantized model support for Turing-generation GPUs and newer, with reworked LoRA and memory handling, plus new nodes including Seed, Advanced Krea 2 Model Merging, Bounding Box Canvas, ConditioningMultiply and an Ideogram JSON prompt node, and support for Google's Nano Banana 2 Lite. It builds on a busy 2026: a full Comfy Desktop overhaul in June brought multi-instance management, snapshots and shared model storage, and the project added Krea2 and LTX2 video models, official AMD ROCm support on Windows, and NVFP4 GPU performance upgrades.

Beyond still images, ComfyUI now drives video generation through models like Krea2 and LTX2, so it is no longer just an image tool. You can chain multiple models, mix custom and community nodes, batch-process, and export whole workflows as reusable JSON.

Pricing has two sides. The self-hosted software is completely free and open-source. The official Comfy Cloud managed service, which left beta and moved to a unified credit model in late 2025 before adding a free tier in March 2026, has a Free plan (400 credits/month, no card required), Standard at $20/month (4,200 credits), Creator at $35/month (7,400 credits, with LoRA import), Pro at $100/month (21,100 credits) and a custom Enterprise tier.

The main limitation is the learning curve. The node graph is powerful but intimidating for beginners, and running locally means managing GPU hardware, model files and dependencies yourself. Comfy Cloud removes the setup burden but ties usage to a credit budget.

Choose ComfyUI if you want deep, reproducible control over generation, are comfortable with a technical interface, or want the option to start free locally and move to a managed cloud later.

before.best_for: AI video editing, voice cloning, dubbing, MCP automation
before.description: Descript is a transcript-based audio and video editor whose current centerpiece is Underlord (2026), a generative AI co-editor that drafts scripts, writes show notes, finds shareable clips, and generates and extends video.
before.description_long:
Descript is an editor for podcasts and video that works off a transcript: you edit the words in a document and the audio and video follow. That approach makes cutting, rearranging, and cleaning up recordings much faster than dragging clips on a traditional timeline.

The product has shifted decisively toward AI. Its headline layer is now Underlord, a generative co-editor that drafts scripts, writes show notes, automatically surfaces viral and social clips, reorganizes scenes, and can generate and extend video on its own. Classic tools like filler-word removal, noise suppression, and timing fixes are still there but are now framed as part of this AI workflow. In 2026 Descript added an AI model picker (including Claude Sonnet 4.5) so you can control reasoning and style, parallel AI media-generation jobs, automatic avoidance of letterbox and crop bars, and a public token-based API open to all users.

On the editing side you get multitrack audio and video, screen recording, layered timelines, remote recording, transcription, and AI voices, plus overdub-style corrections and translation and dubbing features.

Pricing is freemium. There is a Free plan at $0, Hobbyist at $16/user/month billed annually ($24 monthly), Creator at $24/user/month annually ($35 monthly), Business at $50/user/month annually ($65 monthly), and a custom Enterprise tier. In September 2025 the billing model was rebuilt: the old transcription-hours allowance was replaced by monthly media minutes/hours plus metered AI credits, with top-ups available.

The main limitations are cost predictability and dependence on credits. Because AI generation and media time are metered, heavy AI users can burn through their allowance and need top-ups, and the plan structure is more complex than a flat subscription. It is also a fairly heavy app that expects reasonably capable hardware.

Descript suits podcasters, video creators, marketers, and teams who want to edit by editing text and lean on AI for drafting, clipping, and cleanup rather than hand-crafting every cut on a timeline.

before.description_long:
Frase is an AI content and SEO platform aimed at teams that want to rank both in classic search results and inside AI-generated answers. Historically it was known as a research and content-brief tool with the tagline of writing faster with full search context, but that framing no longer describes the product.

In January 2026 Frase was rebuilt from the ground up and relaunched as a GEO-first (Generative Engine Optimization) platform. The old volume metric of documents per month was replaced by AI-Optimized Articles per month.
