before.best_for: Plain language writing — identifies complex sentences and passive voice
before.description: A readability editor that flags hard-to-read sentences, passive voice and adverbs. The current flagship, Hemingway Editor Plus, adds an AI layer with sentence rewrites, grammar fixes and tone adjustment on top of the long-standing free online highlighter.
before.description_long:
Hemingway Editor is a writing tool built around one simple idea: bold, clear prose. It highlights sentences that are hard or very hard to read, marks passive voice, adverbs and overly complex phrases, and gives you a readability grade so you can tighten your text.

The product has shifted well beyond the old free highlighter. The current flagship is Hemingway Editor Plus, a web-based, AI-powered version that sits alongside the free online editor and the one-time-purchase desktop app now called Hemingway Editor Classic. The site also exposes standalone free AI tools such as a proofreader, paraphraser, grammar checker and readability checker.

Capabilities depend on which version you use. The free online editor gives you the classic color-coded readability highlighting with no signup. Plus adds the AI features that are now central to the product: AI sentence rewrites, advanced grammar fixes, tone adjustment, AI synonym suggestions and document feedback.

Pricing is tiered. The online editor is free. Hemingway Editor Plus Individual 5K is $10/month or $100/year (about $8.33/month) and includes 5,000 AI sentence rewrites per month. Individual 10K is $12.50/month billed annually ($150/year) for 10,000 rewrites. Team 10K is $12.50 per user/month ($150/user/year) with 10,000 rewrites per user plus admin controls and priority support. Plus comes with a free two-week trial and no credit card required. The Classic desktop app has historically been a one-time purchase of around $19.99, though that figure is reported by third parties rather than confirmed on the current official pricing pages.

The limitations are worth knowing. The AI rewrites are metered by a monthly quota (5K or 10K), so heavy users can run out. The readability model is opinionated and English-centric, and it can flag perfectly good sentences simply for being long. It is not a full writing suite like a word processor or a research assistant.

Hemingway Editor suits writers, bloggers, students and professionals who want punchier, easier-to-read prose. The free tool is enough for occasional polishing; Plus makes sense if you want AI rewrites and grammar help in one place, and the Classic desktop app fits people who prefer a one-time offline purchase.

before.description: Looker Studio is Google's free-to-start business intelligence tool for building interactive dashboards and reports from more than a thousand data connectors. As a continuously updated SaaS it now embeds Gemini AI, though the most advanced AI features sit behind the paid Pro tier.
before.description_long:
Looker Studio (formerly Google Data Studio) is a web-based reporting and dashboarding platform that turns spreadsheets, databases, ad platforms and Google services into shareable, interactive visualizations. It runs entirely in the browser and needs only a Google account to start.

There is no version number to track; it ships as a continuously updated SaaS. The most significant recent change is the integration of Gemini AI, which brings Conversational Analytics (asking questions of your data in plain language), AI-suggested calculated fields, and the ability to export a report to Google Slides. A January 29, 2026 update added a 'Show reasoning' toggle that exposes the AI's step-by-step logic - which tables it queried, how it grouped and sorted - along with improvements to cross-data filtering.

Core capabilities include drag-and-drop chart building, blended data from multiple sources, calculated fields, filters and controls, scheduled report delivery on Pro, and connectors to over a thousand partner data sources on top of Google's own native ones.

Pricing is split into two tiers. The free tier costs nothing beyond a Google account and gives you unlimited reports and data sources plus core charting, filtering and sharing. Looker Studio Pro is $9 per user per Google Cloud project per month, billed annually with a 30-day trial, and adds organizational ownership, team workspaces, scheduled deliveries, the Gemini AI features, Slack and Google Chat integration, a mobile app and a 99.9% SLA.

The limitations are worth knowing up front. Most of the Gemini AI functionality is gated to Pro, so the free tier is largely a manual dashboarding tool. The Pro pricing is charged per Google Cloud project, which means agencies managing many client projects pay $9 per user for each one, and costs add up quickly. Large or heavily blended reports can also feel sluggish.

Looker Studio suits marketers, analysts and small teams already inside the Google ecosystem who want free, flexible dashboards, and organizations willing to pay for Pro to get governance, scheduling and the AI layer. It is a weaker fit for anyone needing enterprise-grade modeling, which lives in the separate, quote-based Looker product.

before.description: Pika is an AI video generator for turning text prompts and images into short animated clips. Its current model, Pika 2.5 (released January 26, 2026), adds camera-direction control, native scene extension to about 15 seconds, and automatic sound effects synced to the action.
before.description_long:
Pika is a web-based AI tool that creates short video clips from a written prompt or a still image. It's aimed at creators who want quick motion graphics, social clips, and visual experiments without touching traditional video software.

The current flagship model is Pika 2.5, which rolled out on January 26, 2026. Compared to earlier versions it produces sharper footage, gives first-class control over camera moves, extends scenes to roughly 15 seconds natively (and up to about 25 seconds through Pikaframes), and now generates sound effects automatically, matched to what happens on screen.

Beyond generation, Pika is known for Pikaffects, its library of one-tap transformation effects (things like inflating, melting, or crushing objects). Camera direction, resolution options, and image-to-video and text-to-video modes round out the core toolset.

Pricing runs on a credit system. Free is $0 and gives 80 video credits a month, but is now limited to Pika 2.5 at 480p, image-to-video only, and no commercial use. Standard is $8/mo billed yearly (about $10 month-to-month) with 700 credits, all resolutions, every Pikaffect, no watermark, and commercial rights. Pro is $28/mo yearly (about $35 monthly) with 2,300 credits and faster generation, and Fancy is $76/mo yearly (about $95 monthly) with 6,000 credits and the fastest queue. Annual billing saves roughly 20%.

The main limitations are on the free plan: the 480p cap, the image-to-video-only restriction, and the fact that full Pikaffects and higher resolutions are paid features. Credits also deplete quickly if you iterate a lot, and clip lengths remain short by nature.

Pika suits social media creators, marketers, and hobbyists who want fast, playful AI video and are fine with short clips. Anyone needing text-to-video, HD output, commercial use, or the full effects library will need at least the Standard plan.

Its own video model, Pika 2.5, sits alongside third-party video models from vendors such as Google, Seedance, MiniMax, and Wan, image models from vendors including OpenAI, Nano Banana, Seedream, and Grok, and audio tools including Pika's own Speech, Music, and SFX offerings plus ElevenLabs and MiniMax Music.

Pika has repositioned itself from a single video generator into a multi-model creation hub. Alongside the consumer web app at pika.art, the company now offers a developer API at dev.pika.art and an MCP integration for connecting Pika's models into external workflows. Its pricing tiers have also been renamed: the former Standard and Pro plans are now called Starter and Creator.

On the web app, users can generate clips with Pika 2.5 using camera-direction controls, with native clip lengths of about 5 seconds from a text prompt or 5 to 10 seconds from a photo, at 720p or 1080p. A Frames feature stitches together 1-to-5-second transitions between images, extending to about 10 seconds when exactly two frames are used. Renders come back silent by default; audio has to be added afterward with Pika Soundtrack or one of the other audio models on the platform.

Pika runs on a credit system. A free account has 0 monthly credits and requires buying one-off credit packs, priced at roughly 60 credits per dollar from $25 for 1,500 credits up to $1,000 for 66,000, and carries no commercial license. Starter costs $10 per month billed monthly or $8 per month billed annually for 900 credits a month, also without a commercial license. Creator costs $35 per month billed monthly or $28 per month billed annually for 3,150 credits a month and includes a commercial license. Fancy scales from $95 to $880 per month billed monthly, or $76 to $704 per month billed annually, for 8,550 or more credits, with a priority queue and early access to new features. A custom-priced Enterprise plan is also available.

There is no usable free plan: free accounts have no monthly credit allowance and must pay for credit packs to generate anything. Even the paid Starter tier withholds a commercial license, which only arrives at Creator and above. Output remains silent unless paired with a separate audio step, and native clip lengths are short before any extension work.

Pika suits creators and teams who want to try multiple AI video, image, and audio models in a single credit-based platform, including those building through its developer API. Users needing a genuinely free tier or built-in automatic sound effects should look elsewhere.

before.description: Semrush is a marketing and SEO platform for keyword research, competitor analysis, site audits and content optimization. before.description_long:
Semrush is one of the longest-running online-visibility platforms, built around keyword research, rank tracking, backlink and traffic analysis, technical site audits and content tools. Marketers, agencies and SEO teams use it to size up competitors and plan campaigns across search and paid channels.

In 2026 the product was repositioned around AI search. The current lineup, Semrush One, splits into four plans (SEO, Starter, Pro+, Advanced) and bundles the classic SEO toolkit with a new AI Visibility Toolkit that monitors brand mentions across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and Google AI Mode.

Alongside that, Semrush shipped an LLM Gap Analyzer app and Bot and Agent Analytics to show which AI crawlers hit your site, and published an expanded 2026 AI Visibility Index built on 126 million U.S. AI-search prompts.

On annual billing the Semrush One tiers run about $117.33/mo for SEO, $165.17/mo for Starter (which adds AI Visibility and 50 prompts/day), $248.17/mo for Pro+ and $455.67/mo for Advanced; monthly billing pushes the top tier to $549/mo. The classic SEO plans are still sold as Pro ($139.95/mo), Guru ($249.95/mo) and Business ($499.95/mo). A limited free account (around 10 searches a day, first 10 results per report) and a 7-day trial requiring a credit card are available.

The main drawbacks are cost and complexity: entry pricing is high for freelancers, extra seats and add-ons stack up quickly, and the sheer breadth of tools has a real learning curve. The most useful AI-visibility features sit on the paid tiers.

Semrush fits agencies, in-house marketing teams and serious SEO practitioners who want one platform covering both traditional search rankings and the newer question of how a brand surfaces inside AI answers.

before.description: Tableau Agent is the AI assistant built into Tableau (formerly Einstein Copilot for Tableau). It brings conversational, natural-language analytics and agentic authoring to Tableau Cloud, Prep and Catalog, delivered through the Tableau+ bundle.
before.description_long:
Tableau Agent is Salesforce's generative-AI layer inside Tableau. You describe what you want in plain language and it helps build calculations, prep data, suggest visualizations and explain what is happening in a chart, rather than making you click through menus manually.

The product used to be called Einstein Copilot for Tableau and has been rebranded to Tableau Agent. It is now generally available across Tableau Cloud Web Authoring, Tableau Prep and Tableau Catalog. Salesforce has also launched a wider agentic-analytics platform called Tableau Next (also referred to as Tableau Einstein) that the Agent plugs into.

Development through 2026 has been steady: Tableau Agent inside Dashboards entered Beta in February 2026, the Tableau MCP integration became a cloud-hosted service, and a guided setup flow was added to make enabling the AI features less painful for admins.

Pricing is subscription-based with no permanent free tier, though there is a 14-day trial that does not require a credit card. Tableau Cloud Standard (billed annually) runs $75/user/mo for a Creator, $42 for an Explorer and $15 for a Viewer; Tableau Cloud Enterprise is $115, $70 and $35 respectively. The AI capabilities ship inside the Tableau+ bundle, which is quote-only (contact sales) and reportedly lists around $115/user/mo for a Creator. As of October 2025 the AI features no longer burn separate Einstein Request credits.

The main limitations are that it is not a standalone product: you need a Tableau Cloud subscription plus Tableau+ to get the agentic features, real per-seat AI pricing is behind a sales conversation, and the newest pieces (Agent in Dashboards) are still in Beta.

It makes sense for teams already invested in Tableau or the wider Salesforce ecosystem who want natural-language authoring and self-service analytics without hiring more analysts.

Adobe Podcast is a web app for recording and cleaning up spoken-word audio without a traditional editing suite. Its best-known feature, Enhance Speech, strips background noise and room echo from voice recordings and makes them sound as if they were captured with a studio microphone.

The 2026 release, Enhance Speech v2, is a substantial rework. Instead of just removing noise, it performs advanced source separation: you can independently adjust or remove background noise, isolate the dialogue, and raise or lower background music with sliders, then download separate audio stems for speech, noise and music. A new Room Modeling option keeps the natural acoustic character of a space rather than flattening it, and the transformer-based inpainting model rebuilds missing phonemes.

The Studio side of the product now accepts multitrack audio and video uploads with automatic syncing, so podcast and interview recordings from several sources can be aligned and enhanced together.

Pricing is now freemium. The free plan costs nothing but is audio-only with no video, no bulk uploads, files capped at 30 minutes and 500 MB, a one-hour-per-day enhancement limit, and Studio downloads restricted to 30-minute projects, twice a day. Premium is $9.99/month or $99.99/year with a 30-day trial, adding video (MP4/MOV), batch uploads, adjustable speech/music/ambience strength, files up to 1 GB, up to four hours a day, unlimited Studio downloads, speaker-separated stems and Adobe Express Premium design tools.

The main limitation is that the features most people want at scale, video, long files and bulk processing, sit behind Premium, and the free daily caps are easy to hit in a real workflow.

It suits podcasters, interviewers, video creators and anyone who records voice in imperfect rooms and wants clean results fast; the free tier is fine for occasional short clips, while regular producers will need Premium.

before.best_for: AI search across 220M+ academic papers with consensus-finding summaries
before.description: Consensus is an AI research engine that searches a corpus of 220M+ academic papers to answer questions with evidence; its 2026 lineup centers on Deep Search, a Research Agent, and Medical Mode rather than the old "consensus meter" alone.
before.description_long:
Consensus is a search tool built for academic and scientific literature. You ask a question in plain language and it pulls relevant peer-reviewed papers, summarizes what they found, and links directly back to the sources so you can check the claims yourself. It draws on a corpus cited at over 220 million papers.

The product has changed a lot since its early days. It launched around the idea of a "consensus meter" that showed the percentage of studies agreeing with a claim, and while that feature still exists, it is no longer the headline. The 2026 version (no numbered release) is organized around Deep Search and a Research Agent.

Deep Search breaks your question into sub-questions, runs up to roughly 20 targeted searches, and synthesizes across as many as 50 papers, with a wide-coverage mode that can scan up to about 1,000. The Research Agent handles multi-step research questions, Medical Mode restricts sources to clinical guidelines and top medical journals, and an improved MCP lets you use Consensus inside ChatGPT, Codex, Claude, and Claude Code.

Pricing is freemium. Free ($0) gives you basic Quick Search, abstract summaries, limited Pro messages, and about 3 Deep Searches a month. Student is $9/mo with .edu/.ac verification and up to ~40% off annual. Pro is $10/mo for unlimited Pro search, a larger Deep Search allotment, Study Snapshots, and full export (~33% off annual). A higher Deep tier is reported at $45/user/mo with around 200 Deep Searches a month and unlimited snapshots.

The limits are worth knowing. Free Deep Search is capped tightly, so heavy users will hit the paywall quickly. Coverage skews toward what is indexed and abstract-level for some records, and like any AI summarizer it can flatten nuance, so you still need to read the primary sources for anything high-stakes. Note also that an unrelated sales-demo product at goconsensus.com shares the name and costs $600-$1,250/mo; it is not this tool.

It suits researchers, students, clinicians, and analysts who want grounded, citable answers from the literature and are comfortable verifying against the originals rather than trusting a summary at face value.

before.description: Devin is Cognition's autonomous AI software engineer that plans, writes, tests and reviews code largely on its own. The current release is Devin 2.2, now running on the Devin Fusion multi-model architecture with the new Devin Security Swarm for vulnerability fixing.
before.description_long:
Devin is an autonomous coding agent built by Cognition. Rather than sitting inside your editor as a copilot, it works more like a remote engineer: you assign it a task, and it spins up its own cloud workspace with a shell, browser and code editor to plan the work, make changes across the repo, run tests and open a pull request.

The current version is Devin 2.2, released on February 24, 2026. It brought roughly 3x faster session startup, full desktop and computer-use testing, automated code review and a redesigned lifecycle UI. Under the hood Devin now runs the Devin Fusion architecture (announced June 2026), which pairs frontier models with cheaper 'sidekick' agents and claims frontier-level quality at about 35% lower cost than using Opus 4.8 alone. The latest addition is Devin Security Swarm (July 2026), which finds, validates and fixes vulnerabilities. There is no Devin 2.3 yet.

In practice Devin is best at well-scoped, parallelizable work: bug fixes, refactors, migrations, test writing, small features and codebase Q&A. You can run several Devin sessions at once, and it integrates with Slack, GitHub and IDEs so you can hand off tasks and review the resulting PRs.

Pricing was restructured after the Windsurf acquisition into self-serve tiers. Free is $0 with a light agent quota, limited models and unlimited inline edits plus Tab completions. Pro is $20/month with larger quotas, access to OpenAI/Claude/Gemini models, free SWE-1.6 and open-source models, and cloud agents. Max is $200/month for power users, and Teams is $80/month base plus $40/month per developer seat with an admin dashboard and centralized billing. Enterprise is custom and still billed in ACUs (Agent Compute Units) with SSO and optional VPC.

The limitations are the usual autonomous-agent ones: it can burn through quota or credits on ambiguous tasks, sometimes goes down the wrong path and needs redirection, and large or messy codebases still require careful task scoping and human review before merging. Note that many third-party blogs still quote the older ACU-only pricing (Core $20 + $2.25/ACU, Team $500/mo), which the official billing docs indicate has been replaced for self-serve.

Devin suits teams that want to offload routine engineering work to a fleet of parallel agents and are comfortable reviewing PRs, as well as individual developers who want to try autonomous coding without paying up front thanks to the new free tier.

before.description: Gamma is an AI tool for generating presentations, documents, and websites from a prompt. The current release, Gamma 3.0, adds Gamma Agent, a conversational AI that restyles and rewrites decks from natural-language instructions.
before.description_long:
Gamma is a web-based tool that turns a short prompt or an outline into a finished presentation, document, or simple website. Instead of arranging slides by hand, you describe what you want and Gamma builds the structure, writing, and layout for you to refine.

The current version is Gamma 3.0. Its headline addition is Gamma Agent, a conversational AI that restyles and rewrites a deck from plain-language commands rather than manual editing. The release also adds several image models (Nano Banana Pro with in-image text and 4K HD output, Recraft V4, Gemini 3.1 Flash Image, and Flux 2), plus a new Gamma Imagine product for marketing assets, charts, and infographics.

On the capability side, the Claude and ChatGPT connectors were improved to handle deck naming, card counts, brand colors, and plan checks, and Gamma is now available as an app inside ChatGPT. The editor gained 6-column layouts and gradient card backgrounds, and the public API can now delete decks.

Pricing is split into Free, Plus, Pro, and Ultra individual plans, plus Team and Business. The Free plan now grants 400 one-time credits that never refresh, allows 10 cards per prompt, and keeps a Made with Gamma badge. Plus runs about $9/seat/month with roughly 1,000 monthly credits and watermark removal; Pro is about $18/seat/month with around 4,000 credits, custom branding, and API access; the newer Ultra tier is about $90/seat/month with roughly 20,000 credits and top-tier models. Team is about $20/seat/month (annual, two-seat minimum) and Business about $40/seat/month (annual, ten-seat minimum) with SSO and SOC 2.

Limitations are worth noting. Credits are consumed by AI generation, so heavy users can burn through an allowance quickly, and the Free plan's 400 credits do not renew. Exact monthly prices vary by a few dollars across sources, and fine visual control still lags behind traditional design tools.

Gamma suits people who need to produce decks, one-pagers, or landing pages fast and value speed over pixel-level control. It is a strong fit for founders, marketers, educators, and teams that want a consistent house style without a dedicated designer.

before.description: HeyGen is an AI video platform for creating avatar-driven videos, voice cloning and translation. Its current flagship model, Avatar V (May 2026), builds a lifelike digital twin from a 15-second recording.
before.description_long:
HeyGen is a browser-based platform for producing videos that are presented by AI avatars. You type or paste a script, pick or create an avatar, choose a voice, and the system generates a talking-head video without a camera crew or studio.

The current flagship is Avatar V, released in May 2026 and now the most realistic avatar model HeyGen offers. It is created from a single 15-second recording and adds full upper-body motion, multi-angle consistency and long-form identity stability, so the same avatar stays believable across longer scripts. Multi-look generation lets you change outfit or background while preserving the original movement. HeyGen has also integrated Seedance 2.0 for more cinematic AI video generation, and language coverage has grown to 175+ on paid plans (30+ on Free).

Beyond avatars, the core toolkit covers voice cloning, video translation with lip-sync, a library of 500+ stock avatars, and an API for programmatic generation.

Pricing now runs on a credit system across five tiers. Free is $0/mo (3 videos/mo, up to 1 minute each, 1 custom digital twin, 30+ languages). Creator is $29/mo ($24 billed annually) with 600 credits, up to 30-minute videos, 1080p, voice cloning and 175+ languages. Pro is $49/mo with 1,000 credits, 4K and scalable credit tiers. Business is $149/mo plus $20 per extra seat, 1,500 credits, up to 60-minute videos, 5 digital twins, SSO/SAML and LMS. Enterprise is custom.

The main limitation is credit consumption: Avatar IV/V studio videos cost around 20 credits per minute, far faster than older avatars, and lip-sync translation runs about 5 credits per minute, so heavy users burn through allowances quickly. Add-on packs (e.g. 300 credits for $15/mo) and API pricing (~$0.05/second for Avatar V) fill the gap.

HeyGen suits marketers, training teams, localization teams and creators who need frequent talking-head video without filming, and who can work within a credit budget.

before.description: Lovable is an agentic no-code platform that turns plain-language prompts into working web apps. It builds autonomously through a default Agent/Build mode, with a Plan Mode for previewing changes and AI Subagents for parallel work, all metered by a unified credit system.
before.description_long:
Lovable lets you describe an app in everyday language and have it built for you, including the interface, logic, and a managed backend. It is aimed at founders, product people, and developers who want to go from idea to a deployable app without writing everything by hand.

The product has moved to a fully agentic, credit-based model rather than a versioned release cycle. Agent Mode (also called Build mode) is now the default and runs autonomously: it reads your codebase, searches the web, debugs, generates images, and validates its own output. Plan Mode arrived in February 2026 to let you preview intended changes before any code is written, an Agent Mode beta expansion landed in June 2026, and AI Subagents (Researcher, Reviewer, Synthesizer) shipped in May 2026 to run work in parallel.

On capabilities, the backend is now branded Lovable Cloud, a managed layer built on Supabase under the hood, with Lovable AI handling in-app AI features. You get database, auth, and hosting without wiring raw services yourself, plus code editing and custom domains on paid tiers.

Pricing is credit-based across both building and running apps. Free is $0/mo with 5 build credits per day (roughly 30/mo), 20 monthly Cloud credits, and limited in-app AI credits. Pro is $25/mo (about $21/mo billed annually, $250/yr) for 100 monthly credits, private projects, code editing, and custom domains, and scales up to much larger credit tiers. Business is $50/mo with the same 100-credit base plus SSO, data-training opt-out, per-user credit limits, and restricted projects. Enterprise is quote-based with audit logs and SLAs, reportedly around $500+/mo on annual commitment.

The main limitation is the credit model itself: because credits cover building, deployed-app runtime, and in-app AI, costs can be hard to predict on active projects, and the free tier runs out quickly. Autonomous generation is fast but still needs review, and heavy customization eventually pushes you into editing code.

Choose Lovable if you want an AI agent to do most of the building and you are comfortable steering it, and budget for credit consumption if your app is more than a prototype.

before.description: n8n is a fair-code workflow automation platform for connecting apps, APIs and AI agents. The current stable release is the 2.x series (n8n@2.29.8, July 2026), which centers on a rebuilt AI Agent node and a new spatial Canvas editor.
before.description_long:
n8n is a workflow automation tool that lets you wire together apps, databases and APIs through a visual editor, with the option to drop into code when you need it. It runs self-hosted or in the cloud.

The product has moved to the 2.x release line, with n8n@2.29.8 as the current stable build (released July 8, 2026) and 2.30.x in pre-release. The big 2026 change is that AI and agents are now front and center: the AI Agent node was rebuilt with structured tool calling for Claude, GPT-5.6, Gemini, Mistral, Groq and OpenAI-compatible models, four memory backends (in-memory, Redis, Postgres, Motorhead) and a ReAct execution mode. The flat builder was replaced by a spatial Canvas UI introduced in v1.30.

Beyond AI, recent versions add per-node retry with exponential backoff, 35+ new native integrations (including dedicated Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, Groq, Perplexity and ElevenLabs nodes for a total of 500+), expanded admin controls, public API access and more enterprise auth options. Cloud plans now bundle monthly AI credits: 2,300 on Starter, up to 13,700 on Pro.

Pricing is genuinely tiered. The self-hosted Community Edition is free ($0) with unlimited executions and every integration, plus a 14-day cloud trial. Paid cloud tiers run Starter at EUR 24/mo, Pro at EUR 60/mo, Business at EUR 800/mo and custom Enterprise; annual billing is roughly 17% cheaper (about EUR 20, 50 and 667 respectively). A start-up program offers 50% off Business for companies under 20 employees.

The main limitations are honest ones: n8n is fair-code under the Sustainable Use License, not OSI-approved open source, so commercial resale is restricted. Self-hosting means you own the maintenance, and the paid cloud pricing steps up sharply between Pro and Business.

It suits developers and technical teams who want automation they can host and audit themselves, and who increasingly want to build AI-agent workflows without stitching together separate tools.

before.description: Pitch is an AI presentation workspace built around Pitch Agent, a conversational AI that generates fully on-brand decks from a prompt and your files, then rewrites, splits, and refines slides on request. It combines that agent with real-time collaboration and shared brand templates.
before.description_long:
Pitch is a web-based tool for creating and collaborating on presentations. It started as a design-forward alternative to PowerPoint and Google Slides, aimed at teams that want polished decks without fighting with formatting.

As of early July 2026, Pitch has repositioned itself as "The AI presentation workspace," and the headline change is Pitch Agent. Instead of a simple AI writing helper, Pitch Agent is a conversational agent: you describe what you need and upload supporting files, and it drafts a complete presentation using your team's approved templates. You can then ask it to rewrite a section, break up an overcrowded slide, tighten the story, or answer questions about the deck itself.

before.description_long:
UX Pilot is an AI-assisted product design tool aimed at UX/UI designers who want to move from idea to high-fidelity screens quickly. Instead of starting from a blank canvas, you describe what you need and the tool generates full interfaces you can refine.

There is no public model version number. Instead, UX Pilot offers three generation modes: Standard, Deep Design, and Max, which trade higher credit cost for more elaborate output. Through 2026 the product added the Nodey plugin for generating and editing components directly inside Figma, AI UX-research with attention-prediction, and design-to-code that converts an image into HTML. It now runs direct comparison pages against Anthropic's Claude Design (Claude Opus 4.7) and other AI design tools.

Key capabilities include text-to-UI generation, in-Figma editing via Nodey, attention heatmaps and UX-research feedback, and image-to-HTML export for handing work to developers.

Pricing is credit-based. The Free plan is $0 with 45 credits (recent reviews describe these as one-time, not monthly) covering up to about 7 screens. Standard is $14/month billed annually ($19 monthly) with 420 credits, roughly 70 screens. Pro is $22/month billed annually ($29 monthly) with 1,200 credits, around 200 screens, marked Popular. Teams is $31/user/month billed annually ($39 monthly) with 1,600 credits per user, about 266 screens. Enterprise is custom, with unlimited or custom credits and model fine-tuning.

The main limitation is the credit economy: credits do not roll over, and the richer Deep Design and Max modes burn roughly 12 to 18 credits per screen versus about 6 in Standard, so heavy or high-detail use consumes budget fast. The free tier's credits are one-time rather than a recurring allowance.

It suits designers and small teams who want fast AI-generated screens, Figma users who want generation inside their existing workflow, and anyone who needs quick design-to-HTML output. Teams with steady high-volume needs should model the credit burn before committing.

before.best_for: Terminal AI pair programmer with automatic git commits
before.description: Open-source terminal AI pair programmer that auto-commits every change to git, builds a repo map of large codebases, and supports any LLM. 40,000+ GitHub stars and 5 million PyPI installs.
before.description_long:
Aider is an open-source Python-based AI pair programmer that runs entirely in the terminal. Its defining feature is git-native operation: every change the AI makes is automatically committed with a descriptive commit message, so you can use git diff, git log, and git revert to audit or undo any AI modification. This makes it uniquely safe for production codebases where tracking changes matters.

The tool processes 15 billion tokens per week across its user base as of early 2026. Aider builds a repo map — a semantic index of the entire codebase — enabling accurate multi-file edits across large projects. It connects to any LLM: Claude Sonnet, GPT-5.6, Gemini, DeepSeek, local Ollama models, and dozens of providers via OpenRouter. The open-source community releases frequent updates.

Key capabilities include automatic git commits for every AI change, multi-file editing across large codebases via repo map, voice input mode, in-editor image support for visual debugging, and a watch mode that responds to special comments in your code. Aider works in any directory without IDE plugins or configuration beyond an API key.

Pricing: Aider is completely free and open source. You pay only for LLM API calls to your chosen provider. Running on local models via Ollama costs nothing beyond hardware.

Limitations: Aider is terminal-only — there is no GUI, IDE extension, or browser interface. Setup requires installing via pip and configuring an API key. Like all BYOK tools, LLM costs are paid separately.

Best suited for developers who live in the terminal and want an AI pair programmer with full git accountability — where every AI change is tracked, reviewable, and reversible.

before.description: Character.AI is a conversational platform for chatting with user-created AI characters, now running on its DeepSqueak and PipSqueak models (DeepSqueak 2 in training as of April 2026).
before.description_long:
Character.AI is a chat platform built around AI personas: you talk to thousands of user-made characters, from fictional figures to helpers and companions, or build your own. It has long been one of the most-used consumer chat apps outside the big general-purpose assistants.

The service runs on its in-house models: DeepSqueak, the flagship, and PipSqueak, a faster and more efficient option. A successor, DeepSqueak 2, has been in training as of April 2026, and the April 2026 update brought model and memory improvements plus DeepSqueak reliability fixes. For c.ai+ members it also added a Memory Visualization meter and a Lorebook feature for defining persistent world details.

Core capabilities include multi-turn roleplay and storytelling, custom character creation with personas and voices, voice calls, and tools for generating videos, stories and streams. The Lorebook and improved memory help characters stay consistent over longer conversations.

Pricing is freemium. The free tier costs nothing but now shows mid-chat ads by default, runs a slow mode, and uses a Charms virtual currency to gate swipe regenerations. c.ai+ (Plus) is $9.99/month or $94.99/year (about $7.92/mo, roughly 20% off the monthly rate) and removes ads and slow mode, unlocks the latest models, better memory and unlimited voice calls. There is no separate Pro tier on the official pricing page.

The biggest limitation is a policy shift effective November 25, 2025: users under 18 can no longer do open-ended chat or roleplay and are redirected to creating videos, stories and streams, with age verification handled in-house and via Persona (facial recognition or ID as a fallback). This followed lawsuits and regulatory pressure. The free tier has also been materially degraded by ads and the Charms system in 2026.

It suits adults who want character-driven chat and roleplay, creators building interactive personas and stories, and anyone happy to pay $9.99/month for an ad-free experience with the best models. Minors and users wanting an unrestricted free experience should look elsewhere.

before.description: Duolingo's premium AI tier: conversation practice, grammar explanations and roleplay scenarios powered by current GPT models. $29.99/mo or $168/yr. Note: Video Call and Explain My Answer are now free for all Duolingo users.
before.description_long:
Duolingo Max is the premium subscription tier that sits above the free plan and the mid-level Super plan. It keeps everything Duolingo is known for — gamified lessons, streaks, and bite-sized practice — and layers AI conversation tools on top for learners who want to actually speak the language.

The AI features originally launched on GPT-4 in 2023 but are now reported to run on OpenAI's GPT-5.6. The current marquee feature is Video Call: a live spoken conversation with an animated character named Lily who remembers details across sessions. It has expanded to more languages, including Japanese, Korean and Chinese. Note that in January 2026, 'Explain My Answer' stopped being a Max exclusive and became free for everyone, so Max's paid edge now rests mainly on Video Call and Roleplay.

Key capabilities include real-time spoken practice with Lily, Roleplay scenarios (ordering food, booking a hotel) where the AI plays a conversation partner, and the usual full Duolingo course library with no ads.

Pricing is tiered: the free plan is $0, Super is $95.99/year, and Duolingo Max is $167.99/year or $29.99/month. There is also a Super Family plan from $119.99/year covering up to six people, though that is Super rather than Max.

Limitations are worth weighing. Max costs almost double Super, and with 'Explain My Answer' now free, the differentiation is narrower than it once was. Video Call availability still depends on your target language, and the AI conversations, while useful, are scripted enough that they don't replace a human tutor for nuance.

Max makes sense if you're already committed to Duolingo, want spoken conversation practice, and are learning a language where Video Call is supported. Casual learners are usually fine on the free tier or Super.

before.best_for: AI coding in VS Code, cloud agents, code review metrics
before.description: GitHub Copilot is an agentic, multi-model coding assistant that goes well beyond autocomplete, offering chat, an autonomous agent mode, cloud agents, code review and a CLI, with user-selectable frontier models. Since June 1, 2026 it runs on usage-based GitHub AI Credits, and pricing spans a free tier up to individual and organization plans.
before.description_long:
GitHub Copilot started as an in-editor autocomplete tool, but the current 2026 product is a full multi-model coding platform. It lives inside your editor, in the terminal and on GitHub itself, handling code completion, chat, an agent mode that edits across files, cloud agents that work on tasks asynchronously, and automated code review.

The biggest recent change came on June 1, 2026, when Copilot moved from premium request units to consumption-based GitHub AI Credits, a token-based system. Every plan now includes a monthly credit allowance, with pay-as-you-go overages and new admin budget and spending caps. The older automatic fallback to cheaper models was discontinued, and code review now also consumes GitHub Actions minutes.

The core capabilities today are agent mode, cloud agents, chat, code review, a CLI, and the ability to pick which frontier model you want, including Claude Sonnet 5, Claude Opus 5, GPT-5.6 and Gemini 3.6 Flash. Code completions and Next Edit suggestions stay included and do not draw down your credit allowance.

On pricing, individuals can choose Free at 0 dollars a month (around 2,000 completions, limited chat and agent use, automatic model selection), Pro at 10 dollars a month (unlimited completions, model selection, cloud agents, a monthly credit allowance), Pro+ at 39 dollars a month (premium frontier models including Opus and a higher allowance), or Max at 100 dollars a month (the highest allowance and priority access to new models). Verified students get Pro-level access free. Organizations pick Business at 19 dollars per user a month (including 19 dollars of monthly AI Credits) or Enterprise at 39 dollars per user a month (including 39 dollars of credits, codebase indexing and GitHub.com chat). Promotional bonus credits run June through August 2026: Business plus 30 dollars a month, Enterprise plus 70 dollars a month.

The main limitation is cost predictability: usage-based billing means heavy agent, chat or frontier-model use can push you into overages, and code review burning Actions minutes adds a second meter to watch. Budgets and caps help, but teams need to monitor consumption.

Copilot is a strong fit if you already work in GitHub and VS Code, want an agentic assistant rather than plain autocomplete, and value being able to choose the underlying model. The free tier is a low-risk way to try it, while Pro+ and Max suit heavier users of premium models.

before.best_for: AI image generation, text-in-image, face swap, canvas editing
before.description: Ideogram is a text-to-image generator known for rendering readable text inside images. The current flagship, Ideogram 4.0 (released June 3, 2026), is the company's first open-weight model and adds native transparency, in-image editing and structured prompting.
before.description_long:
Ideogram is an AI image generator that has built its reputation on one hard problem most rivals still struggle with: putting legible, correctly spelled text into a picture. That makes it a go-to tool for logos, posters, mockups, social graphics and anything where words matter as much as the visuals.

The current version is Ideogram 4.0, released on June 3, 2026. It is the company's first open-weight foundation model, a 9.3B-parameter release under the Apache 2.0 license, and it topped the DesignArena open-weight leaderboard. It succeeds Ideogram 3.0 from March 2025 and is built around structured JSON prompting, tighter typography and layout control, and 2K-class resolutions.

Beyond text rendering, 4.0 adds capabilities the earlier entry lacked: native transparency (usable PNGs with no background), reliable in-image editing, style references to keep a consistent look, and API access for batch and programmatic work.

Pricing is freemium. The free plan costs $0 and gives roughly 10 slow credits per week with public generations and one concurrent job. Basic runs about $8/mo (around $7 billed annually) for ~400 priority credits. Plus is about $20/mo (roughly $15-16 annually) with ~1,000 credits and private images. Pro is about $60/mo (around $42-48 annually) with ~3,000-3,500 credits plus batch generation and API access. A Team plan is about $30/user/mo (around $20 annually) with ~1,500 credits per user, and Enterprise is custom. API usage is billed separately at roughly $0.03-$0.10 per image.

The limitations are worth knowing. The free tier is slow and makes your images public, credits run out faster than heavy users expect, and while text is excellent, photorealism and fine anatomy can lag behind some competitors. API costs add up at volume.

Choose Ideogram if your work centers on typography-heavy visuals, or if you want an open-weight model you can build on. If you mainly need photorealistic scenes with no text, a different generator may serve you better.

before.best_for: Complex automations, app integrations
before.description: Make is a visual, no-code automation platform for building workflows across 3,000+ apps. In its current 2026 form it runs on credit-based billing (operations were renamed to credits on Aug 27, 2025) and ships Make AI Agents, a native feature for building autonomous AI agents inside scenarios.
before.description_long:
Make (formerly Integromat) is a visual automation platform where you connect apps and services on a drag-and-drop canvas to build workflows, called scenarios, without writing code. Each scenario is a chain of modules that pass data from one app to the next, with branching, filters, iterators and error handling.

Make no longer uses traditional version numbers; instead it evolves continuously. The two biggest recent shifts define its current state. First, on August 27, 2025 the billing unit changed from operations to credits (converted 1:1), moving Make toward usage-based pricing where an AI or code step can cost more than a single credit. Second, Make AI Agents became generally available, letting you build autonomous agents directly inside scenarios, backed by an AI Agents Library and 350+ AI-specific app integrations.

On the capability side, Make now advertises 3,000+ app integrations, real-time and scheduled triggers, webhooks, HTTP/API modules, data stores, and reusable custom variables. On paid plans you can bring your own OpenAI, Anthropic or Gemini API keys to power AI steps.

Pricing is tiered. Free is $0/mo with 1,000 credits, a cap of 2 active scenarios and a 15-minute minimum scheduling interval. Core is $9/mo on annual billing (10,000 credits, unlimited scenarios, 1-minute interval). Pro is $16/mo annual, adding priority execution and custom variables. Teams is $29/mo annual with multi-user roles. Enterprise is custom-priced. Monthly billing runs roughly 15-20% higher (about $10.59 Core, $18.82 Pro, $34.12 Teams), and credit packs (20k/40k/80k+) extend limits.

The main limitations are practical. Credit-based pricing makes AI-heavy scenarios harder to forecast, the free tier's 2-scenario cap and 15-minute interval are tight for real work, and the visual model still has a learning curve once scenarios grow complex with nested routers and error handlers.

Make suits people who want a powerful visual automation tool without code, and who now want to layer AI agents into those automations rather than glue together separate services.

Unlike text-to-image tools that generate from scratch, Nano Banana specializes in in-context editing: you upload a photo, describe the changes in plain language, and the model applies them while preserving the original composition, lighting and scene structure.

The standout feature is character consistency. Most AI image tools struggle to keep the same face, outfit or object looking identical across multiple edits or scenes. Nano Banana was built specifically to solve this — making it the go-to tool for serialized content creators, AI influencers, branded campaigns and game asset pipelines where visual coherence across images is non-negotiable.

The free tier offers credits on sign-up with no install required — everything runs in the browser. Nano Banana Pro unlocks 4K resolution, advanced multi-step editing, sharp text rendering and higher-volume generation. For designers, marketers and content creators who need precise, repeatable AI image editing — Nano Banana delivers results competing tools consistently struggle to match.

before.description: Prezi is a presentation tool now built around Prezi AI, which generates a fully designed deck from a single prompt or a document in seconds. Its 2026 lineup also includes Swoop, a standalone AI agent that turns inputs from tools like Drive, Slack and Gmail into presentations, docs and messages.
before.description_long:
Prezi started as the app known for its zoomable, non-linear canvas, but the product most people use today is Prezi AI. Instead of just helping with layout, it builds an entire designed presentation from a one-line prompt or an uploaded document, usually in under about eight seconds and without forcing you through a separate outline step.

There are no formal version numbers for the consumer product anymore; Prezi ships continuously. The big shift is the move from a simple AI design assistant to full generative creation. You can paste a website URL and Prezi will pull the brand's colors, fonts and logo (it recognizes over 2,000 brand logos), then refine the deck through a chat interface with a rewind button to undo changes.

On capabilities, current Prezi AI generates funnels, roadmaps, processes and quote layouts, embeds YouTube video directly in slides, and now exports finished decks to PowerPoint (.PPTX) and PDF. The headline 2026 launch is Swoop, released on March 31, 2026: a standalone AI communication agent at swoop.it that aggregates many sources, Google Drive, Notion, Slack, Gmail, Zoom, Salesforce, HubSpot and meeting recordings, into presentations, documents and messages. Swoop also appears in the Grammarly and Superhuman Go Agent Store.

Pricing is freemium and billed annually. Basic is free but limits you to public presentations. Standard runs about $7 per user per month, Plus about $15, Premium about $25, and Teams about $39 per user per month. Education plans start around $3-4 per month, with EDU Teams near $19 per user per month, and paid plans include a 14-day free trial.

The main limitations are practical. The free tier keeps your work public, which rules it out for anything confidential. Exact prices also vary noticeably across third-party listings, so confirm the current figures on prezi.com before committing, and the zooming style, while distinctive, is not what every audience or corporate template expects.

Prezi suits people who want a designed deck fast without starting from a blank slide, teams that value on-brand output pulled straight from a URL, and anyone curious about Swoop's cross-app agent approach to turning scattered inputs into finished communication.

after.best_for: Live-session audience engagement and post-session learning content, with AI deck creation as an alternate starting point
after.description: Prezi is a presentation platform now built around audience engagement during a live session (polls, quizzes, Q&A, word clouds via one QR code) and post-session learning content (flashcards, self-tests, podcast, narrated video), with AI deck generation offered as one of two ways to start a presentation. Swoop, a separate AI agent built by Prezi, turns inputs from tools like Drive, Slack, Notion and Zoom into presentations and documents.
after.description_long:
Prezi has repositioned itself as, in its own words, the presentation platform built for what happens after you present. There are two ways to start: import an existing file from PowerPoint, Google Slides, Canva or PDF, or describe a topic and let the AI generate a deck. During a live session, presenters can pull in audience input through live polls, quizzes, Q&A and word clouds, all accessible to the audience via a single QR code.

After the session ends, Prezi can turn the material into flashcards, self-tests, a podcast, or a narrated video, all generated from one shareable link. The product ships continuously with no formal version numbers, and this emphasis on engagement and post-session learning marks a clear shift away from the AI-deck-generation-first pitch Prezi used in earlier years.

On the deck side, Prezi AI can still generate funnels, roadmaps, processes and quote layouts, embed YouTube video directly in slides, and export finished decks to PowerPoint (.PPTX) and PDF. A brand kit feature lets you paste a company URL to pull in colors, fonts and a logo for on-brand output. Swoop, built by Prezi and run from a separate site (swoop.it), is the standalone AI agent in the lineup: it connects to tools including Google Drive, Notion, Slack and Zoom and turns their content into presentations and documents, with PowerPoint and PDF export and an MCP/Claude connection. Swoop runs on a credits model, with paid plans including a monthly credit allowance and purchased credits that do not expire.

Prezi's homepage advertises a way to get started for free with no credit card required, alongside multiple paid tiers for individuals, teams and education use; the pricing page itself is rendered entirely in JavaScript and does not expose plan costs in a form that could be verified, so specific dollar figures and free-tier limits are not listed here. Swoop's own paid pricing was also not verified.

The main limitations are practical: you cannot easily check current prices or exact free-tier restrictions without visiting the live, JS-rendered pricing pages, the lack of version numbers makes it hard to track what changed and when, the signature zooming canvas is not to every audience's taste, and Swoop is a separate product from Prezi's core app, splitting the AI workflow across two destinations rather than one.

Prezi now suits presenters who want to turn a live session into an interactive, two-way event and extend it into study or review material afterward, as well as anyone who wants a quick AI-generated deck as an alternative to importing existing slides, or who is curious about Swoop's cross-app approach to building presentations and documents from scattered sources.

before.description: Softr is an AI-native no-code platform for building web apps, client portals and internal tools. Since its March 2026 relaunch, its AI Co-Builder generates a full app - database, interface, permissions and logic - from a plain-language description.
before.description_long:
Softr is a no-code platform for building web applications, client portals, internal tools and simple business software without writing code. You describe what you need or assemble it from prebuilt blocks, and Softr handles the hosting, user accounts and permissions.

On March 31, 2026 Softr relaunched as an AI-native platform. The headline change is the AI Co-Builder, which turns a plain-language description into a working app complete with a database, user interface, access rules and basic business logic. Earlier in 2026 the platform added multi-model AI support (Claude, GPT and Gemini), and in June 2026 it introduced AI-driven web scraping and search. Global Search across apps arrived in December 2025.

A notable capability is that each Softr app can now act as its own Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. That means assistants like Claude and ChatGPT can connect over OAuth and read or act on your app's data directly. Softr also has its own built-in Softr Databases with tiered record limits, so you are no longer tied to Airtable or Google Sheets, though those connections still work.

Pricing is subscription-based with monthly AI credits bundled into every plan. The Free tier is $0/mo (10 app users, 5 AI credits, roughly 1,000-5,000 records). Basic is $49/mo billed annually ($59 monthly) with 20 users and 10 credits. Professional is $139/mo annually ($167 monthly) for 100 users (add-on packs of 10 at $10/mo up to 250) and 50 credits. Business is $269/mo annually ($323 monthly) for 500 users and 100 credits. Enterprise is custom with SSO, advanced security and dedicated support. Extra AI credits run $10-$500/mo for 100-5,000 credits.

The trade-offs are real. AI credits are consumed by generation and AI features, so heavy use pushes you into add-ons or higher tiers quickly. Deep custom design and complex logic still hit the ceiling of a no-code tool, and pricing climbs steeply as your user count grows.

Softr fits non-technical teams and small businesses that want to ship a portal or internal tool fast, and anyone curious about connecting their app data to AI assistants via MCP without building a backend.

before.description_long:
v0 by Vercel is an AI agent for building web apps. You describe what you want in natural language (optionally attaching screenshots or Figma-style references), and it produces working code you can preview, edit, and ship. It is developed by Vercel, the company behind Next.js and the Vercel hosting platform.

The current version is the post-February 2026 "new v0", which changed the product substantially. before.description_long:
Akkio is an AI analytics platform aimed at media and advertising agencies. Rather than a general dashboard tool, it packages a suite of AI agents that handle the repetitive analytical work behind campaign planning, audience segmentation and reporting.

The product has changed direction. Akkio started life as a no-code AI/ML tool for business analysts building forecasting models from CSV or CRM data. As of mid-2026 it has repositioned squarely around agency workflows, and forecasting is now just one capability among many. There are no formal version numbers; the notable recent addition is the Media Planning Agent, which lets you upload reach curves, set goals and generate a baseline media mix you can edit inline.

The agent suite covers the main stages of agency work: an Audience Agent for segmentation, a Strategy Agent, Chat Explore and Chat Data Prep for conversational analysis and cleanup, Forecasting, and Generative Reports that write up findings automatically.

On pricing, the official site now shows only an Enterprise AI Analytics Platform with custom, contact-sales pricing and no public figures. Third-party directories still list older self-serve tiers: a view-only Free plan, Basic at $49/user/month, Pro at $99/user/month, and a Build-On package from $999/month with white-label and API access. A free trial is referenced, but since Akkio no longer publishes these amounts their current accuracy is uncertain.

The main limitations are the narrowed focus and the pricing opacity. If you are not an agency, the media-centric agents may be more than you need, and the shift to contact-sales makes it hard to gauge cost without a sales conversation.

Akkio suits media and advertising agencies that want to automate audience, planning and reporting work with AI agents, and enterprises comfortable with custom contracts. Analysts wanting a simple self-serve forecasting tool may find the product has moved past that use case.

before.description_long:
ChatGPT is OpenAI's flagship chat assistant for writing, coding, research, analysis and multimodal tasks. It works in the browser, in desktop and mobile apps, and through the API, and it has become one of the most widely used consumer AI products in the world.

As of July 2026 the default model is the GPT-5.6 family — Sol, Terra and Luna — offered in Instant and Thinking modes, with a Pro variant on higher tiers. GPT-5.6 launched in July 2026 and replaced the GPT-5.5 lineup; the model picker was simplified to Instant, Thinking and Pro. The GPT-4o era is over, and GPT-4o is no longer the flagship. A newer GPT-5.6 family (Sol flagship, Terra balanced, Luna fast) has entered limited preview but is not yet generally available.

Capabilities cover long-form and technical writing, code generation and debugging, document and image analysis, voice conversations, web browsing, data analysis, and image generation, all built on the current multimodal GPT-5.x stack rather than the older GPT-4o pipeline. Higher tiers add larger context windows and Sora video generation.

Pricing is tiered. Free is $0/mo and now shows ads to logged-in adult users in the US (since February 2026), with the default GPT-5.6 model at limited usage. The new Go tier is $8/mo and has rolled out worldwide. Plus is $20/mo. Pro is now split into two options: $100/mo with roughly 5x Plus quotas, and $200/mo with about 20x quotas plus Sora video and a 1M-token context window. Business (Team) is $25/user/mo with a two-seat minimum, and Enterprise is custom-priced.

Limitations remain real. The model can still produce confident but wrong answers, free usage is capped and now ad-supported in the US, and the most useful capabilities (long context, video, heavy quotas) sit behind the pricier tiers. GPT-5.6 is preview-only, so you cannot rely on it for production yet.

ChatGPT suits almost anyone who wants a general-purpose AI assistant, from casual users on the free or Go tier to professionals and teams who need higher quotas, larger context and collaboration features.

Instead of a single proprietary model, it routes work across leading third-party models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google (Gemini).

Core capabilities now split in two: a chat interface for everyday drafting (ads, emails, posts, briefs) and multi-step Workflows and agents that automate repetitive go-to-market tasks such as lead enrichment, account research and outbound sequences. There are still some free standalone tools and templates on the site, but no free product plan.

The main limitations are the pricing cliff between Chat and the team tiers, and the credit-metered workflows that can make heavier automation expensive to budget. Solo copywriters may also feel the tool has drifted away from them.

Copy.ai suits sales and marketing teams that want to automate go-to-market work with agents and workflows, and can justify team pricing. Individual writers who just want cheap copy generation have better-value options elsewhere.

before.description_long:
Elicit is a research intelligence platform built for academics, evidence synthesis teams, and anyone doing serious literature work. It searches a corpus of more than 138 million papers and 545,000 clinical trials, summarizes findings, lets you chat with papers, and pulls specific data points into structured tables.

The tool has changed significantly. What began as a paper-search and extraction assistant is now a broader platform. Research Agents launched in late 2025 to automate multi-step review workflows, and in March 2026 Elicit released a public API so teams can embed its search, extraction, and report generation into their own tools. The underlying language model was upgraded for more accurate, context-aware summaries and better citation handling.

The core paid offering centers on systematic literature review and data extraction: you can screen thousands of papers, define custom extraction columns, and generate structured reports with sources you can verify.

Pricing is tiered. The Free plan costs $0 and includes unlimited search, unlimited summaries, unlimited chat-with-papers, source viewing and Zotero import, with limited Research Agent and Report usage. Pro is $49/month (or $588/year) and covers standard agent, report, and systematic-review usage, screening up to 5,000 papers, 20 table columns, extraction from up to 135 sources, 10 alerts, and API access. Scale is $169/month (or $2,028/year) with 5x usage, figure extraction, live collaboration, up to 200 sources and admin controls. Enterprise is custom-priced with 40,000-paper screening, PRISMA-grade accuracy, SSO/SAML/2FA and unlimited API.

Limitations are worth noting: the tool is tuned for academic and clinical literature rather than general web research, serious extraction and screening volumes require a paid plan, and as with any AI summarizer, extracted claims and citations still need human verification.

Elicit is a strong fit for researchers, PhD students, systematic reviewers, and R&D or clinical teams who need to move quickly through large bodies of evidence without losing the ability to trace every claim back to its source.

before.description: Glide is a no-code platform for building internal business apps from a spreadsheet, a prompt, or a file. In 2026 it repositioned as GlideOS, an AI-native app development platform, with Glide Agent (an AI app-building assistant) now in beta for new teams.
before.description_long:
Glide is a no-code tool for building internal business applications. You connect a data source, arrange records into screens and lists, and publish a working web app without writing code.

In 2026 Glide rebranded its core product as GlideOS and put AI at the center. It now pitches itself as an AI software development platform that can generate an app from a spreadsheet, a text prompt, or an uploaded file. Glide Agent, its AI app-building assistant, is in beta for all new teams, and Glide also markets enterprise generative-AI agents for operations work.

On capabilities, Glide lets you build list, detail, form, dashboard and kanban-style screens, add roles and row-level access, run automation flows, and use its own Glide Tables as a database. External sources such as Google Sheets, Airtable, Excel and SQL are supported, but availability depends on your plan.

Pricing was restructured on Nov 1, 2025 into five tiers. Free is $0/mo (1 editor, 10 personal users, 25,000 rows, Glide Tables only, no automation updates). Explorer is $19/mo billed annually ($25 monthly): 2 editors, 100 users, 250 updates. Maker is $49/mo annually ($60 monthly): 2 editors, unlimited users, 500 updates, 50,000 rows. Business is $199/mo annually ($249 monthly): 10 editors, 30 users, 5,000 updates, 100,000 rows, plus $5-6 per extra user and $0.02 per extra update. Enterprise is custom (up to 10M rows, 100+ data sources, SSO).

The main limitation is that the entry tiers are narrower than they look. The Free plan only works with Glide Tables, so connecting Google Sheets needs Maker ($49/mo) and Airtable needs Business ($199/mo). Automation updates are metered on every paid plan, which can push active teams up a tier.

Glide fits teams that need internal tools such as inventory, CRM, field data collection or approval workflows fast, and that are comfortable prototyping with AI. It is less suited to consumer-facing apps at scale or to teams that want unmetered automation on a cheap plan.

before.description_long:

The underlying model changed significantly in 2026. Meta AI no longer runs on Llama 4; since the April 8, 2026 announcement it is powered by Muse Spark, the first proprietary large language model from Meta Superintelligence Labs. This was a notable and controversial move away from Meta's open-weight Llama lineage. In July 2026 Meta added Muse Image, its first in-house image-generation model, to Meta AI.

Day to day, the assistant answers questions, drafts and rewrites text, summarizes threads, helps in group chats, and now generates images through Muse Image. Because it lives inside the apps, it can act on the context you are already looking at instead of forcing you into a separate window.

The main limitations are the ones that come with a closed, platform-bound assistant: the shift to the proprietary Muse Spark ended the open-weight approach many developers relied on, availability of paid tiers is still rolling out by country, and Meta AI is tied to Meta's ecosystem rather than being a standalone tool you can host yourself.

It is a natural fit if you already live in WhatsApp, Instagram or Messenger and want an assistant right there, and are fine with a proprietary model and Meta's data practices. If you specifically want open weights or a standalone workspace, look elsewhere.

after.description_long:
Meta AI is the conversational assistant that Meta ships across its apps rather than as a standalone product. You reach it inside WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, Messenger and Threads, and through Meta's AI glasses, so it sits wherever people already chat and browse.

The underlying model changed in 2026. Since an April 8, 2026 announcement, Meta AI runs on Muse Spark, the first proprietary large language model from Meta Superintelligence Labs, replacing the earlier Llama-based engine. In September 2026 Meta also launched Muse, a separate personal AI agent app also powered by Muse Spark, available at muse.ai and through WhatsApp with a US rollout.

Day to day, the assistant answers questions, drafts and rewrites text, summarizes threads, and helps in group chats, acting on the context you are already looking at instead of forcing you into a separate window.

Meta states that the core Meta AI experience remains free for everyday use. On September 15, 2026, Meta launched Meta One worldwide, a subscription system that adds more usage of compute-heavy AI features. It includes single-app "Plus" plans for WhatsApp, Instagram or Facebook, multi-app consumer bundles called Meta One Core and Meta One Premium, and business/creator tiers called Essential, Advanced, Expert and Max. Meta's own published prices are in euros; US-dollar figures circulating for these tiers come from third-party reports and are not confirmed on Meta's primary pricing pages.

The main limitations are the ones that come with a closed, platform-bound assistant: the shift to the proprietary Muse Spark ended the open-weight approach many developers relied on, the tier structure and naming are more complex now that single-app and multi-app plans coexist, and Meta AI is tied to Meta's ecosystem rather than being a standalone tool you can host yourself.

It is a natural fit if you already live in WhatsApp, Instagram or Messenger and want an assistant right there, and are fine with a proprietary model and Meta's data practices. If you specifically want open weights or a standalone workspace, look elsewhere.

before.best_for: AI research notebook — ask questions and generate Audio Overviews from your sources
before.description: NotebookLM is Google's AI research assistant that grounds its answers in your own sources. After the June 2026 "NotebookLM 2.0" upgrade it runs on Gemini 3.5, gives each notebook a cloud computer that writes and runs code, and produces audio and video overviews plus exports to PPT, Excel, PDF, CSV and JSON.
before.description_long:
NotebookLM is a research and note-taking tool from Google. You upload your own material — PDFs, documents, slides, web pages, notes — and it answers questions, summarizes, and builds study aids using only those sources, with citations back to the original text.

The big change came on June 8, 2026, when the "NotebookLM 2.0" upgrade rolled out globally. The product now runs on Gemini 3.5 (plus Google's "Antigravity" models) and has shifted from a static document Q&A tool into a more agentic research assistant. Google reports roughly a 65% average win rate over the previous version, and higher scores on large-document analysis and source discovery.

Capabilities expanded considerably. Each notebook now gets a secure cloud computer that can write and execute code natively for data analysis, drawing on 100+ curated software skills. You can export to editable PDFs with charts and tables, PowerPoint, Excel, and CSV/JSON, and generate images. Video Overviews now sit alongside the familiar Audio Overviews and podcast-style summaries, and integrated web search lets you start a project from an idea rather than only from files you already have.

Pricing is tiered. There is a free Standard tier at $0, then Plus at $7.99/mo (Google AI Plus), Pro at $19.99/mo (Google AI Pro), and Ultra at $99.99/mo and $200/mo (Google AI Ultra). NotebookLM is sold only as part of a Google AI, Workspace, or Cloud plan — you cannot buy it on its own.

The main caveats: the most advanced features were initially gated to the AI Ultra and Workspace business tiers, so the free plan is more limited than the headline announcements suggest. And because answers are grounded in your uploaded sources, the tool is only as good as the material you give it.

It suits students, researchers, analysts, and knowledge workers who need reliable, cited answers over a defined body of documents rather than open-ended web chat.

before.best_for: AI paraphrasing, summarizing, and grammar checking for students and writers
before.description: QuillBot has grown from a paraphrasing and summarizing tool into a full AI writing suite, adding an AI Chat, an AI Presentation Maker, a PDF toolkit, an AI Image Detector, a macOS app and a rebranded interface in 2026.
before.description_long:
QuillBot started life as a paraphraser and quickly became known for its summarizer, grammar checker, plagiarism and AI detectors, translator and citation generator. For years most people used it to reword text or shorten long passages.

In 2026 it is a broader platform. The company reworked its AI Chat, introduced a prompt-to-design, goal-first workflow, and shipped an AI Presentation Maker that turns a prompt into slide decks. It also added a PDF suite (document Q&A, editing, merging, splitting and format conversion), a free AI Image Detector, and a native macOS desktop app, alongside a full UI rebrand. QuillBot does not use formal version numbers.

On the core writing side, the Paraphraser now includes an Academic Mode aimed at scholarly phrasing, and the Summarizer gained a Custom Mode for more control over output. Grammar checking, translation across dozens of languages, and the plagiarism and AI-content detectors remain part of the package.

Pricing is freemium. The free tier costs nothing but caps the paraphraser at 125 words and limits other tools. Premium is $19.95/month, $39.95/quarter or $99.95/year, unlocking longer inputs and the full mode lineup. A Team plan is available by custom quote.

The main limitations: the free plan's word caps are restrictive for regular work, the AI and plagiarism detectors are not authoritative and shouldn't be treated as proof, and the sheer number of tools can feel scattered compared with a focused editor.

QuillBot suits students, writers and non-native English speakers who want paraphrasing, summarizing and grammar help in one place, and who now also want chat, presentations and PDF tools without paying for separate apps.

before.description: Speechify is a text-to-speech and voice-AI platform built on its proprietary SIMBA 3.x model (SIMBA 3.0 reached general availability in March 2026). It reads text aloud in 1000+ voices at up to 5x speed and now adds a Voice AI Assistant, AI Podcasts, Voice Typing, and a developer Voice API.
before.description_long:
Speechify started as a tool that turns written text into spoken audio, and it is still widely used to read articles, PDFs, emails, and documents out loud. Over time it has grown well beyond a simple screen reader.

The biggest change came in 2026, when Speechify moved to its own SIMBA 3.x voice model developed in its AI Voice Research Lab. SIMBA 3.0 reached general availability in March 2026, and the SIMBA 3.2 streaming variant now sits at the top of the Voice Arena leaderboard while powering both the consumer app and the Voice API. This shifted the product from a text reader toward a broader voice-AI platform.

On the capability side, you get text-to-speech in over 1000 voices, reading speeds up to 5x, and a set of newer voice-first features: a Voice AI Assistant, AI Podcasts, Voice Typing, and voice chat. There are also licensed celebrity voices such as Snoop Dogg, MrBeast, and Gwyneth Paltrow. For developers, the Voice API exposes the same SIMBA models, including real-time speech-to-speech and speech recognition.

Pricing follows a freemium model. The Free tier costs nothing and covers basic reading. Premium is $29 per month, or roughly $139 per year on the annual plan, and unlocks the full voice library, higher speeds, and premium voices. Speechify Studio and the Voice API are priced separately, with API pricing around $6 per million characters.

The limitations are worth noting. The most natural voices and useful speeds are gated behind Premium, the celebrity voices are novelty features rather than core tools, and the monthly plan is expensive unless you commit annually. Free users hit fairly quick limits on high-quality voices.

Speechify fits people who consume a lot of written content by ear, students and professionals who want faster reading, and developers who need a modern TTS or speech-to-speech API without building their own model.
